title: Serre criterion for affineness
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs global functions from the H1 vanishing hypothesis and obtains affine principal neighbourhoods. It then combines a finite principal-open cover with a unit-ideal argument to prove affineness; the covering construction is part of the problem rather than an assumed affineness criterion.

title: Chow lemma for separated finite-type morphisms over a Noetherian base
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a quasi-projective proper modification of a separated finite-type scheme over a Noetherian base using closures of diagonal graph maps. Scheme-theoretic density permits gluing the local projections and proves exact inverse-image identities; these verify properness, surjectivity and a dense-open isomorphism. This is a substantive geometric construction beyond routine qualifying algebra.

title: Cohen structure theorem
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs coefficient fields or Cohen coefficient rings by successive lifting. It treats mixed characteristic separately and produces the required surjection from a power-series ring, rather than presupposing a coefficient ring.

title: Stein factorization with geometrically connected fibres
difficulty_reason: The relative spectrum of the direct image gives a finite factorization, but the proof must also establish geometrically connected fibres. The included normalization and proper-fibre arguments carry the nontrivial part of this claim.

title: Skolem-Noether conjugacy theorem
difficulty_reason: The author uses the structure of simple modules and their centralizers to compare two embeddings into a central simple algebra. An isomorphism of the resulting module structures is converted to inner conjugacy, with the module-structure lemmas retained.

title: Lazard characterization of flat modules
difficulty_reason: The proof turns finite relations in a flat module into factorizations through finite free modules. These factorizations construct a directed system whose colimit is the original module, proving the nontrivial direction of Lazard characterization.

title: Miracle flatness
difficulty_reason: The dimension equality permits the choice of an element that is a regular parameter of the source and a nonzerodivisor of the Cohen-Macaulay target. Quotienting lowers both dimensions, allowing induction, and the local flatness criterion then lifts flatness from the quotient.

title: Openness of fibrewise exactness for finite free complexes over flat finite-type algebras over a Noetherian base with Cohen-Macaulay fibres of fixed dimension
difficulty_reason: The author spreads exactness from one localized fibre through determinantal rank bounds and converts the remaining grade conditions into regular-sequence conditions in the fibres. Cohen-Macaulay dimensional control makes these conditions open, giving a substantive family-wise exactness criterion beyond ordinary module exactness tests.

title: Decomposition and classification of injective modules over a Noetherian ring
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a direct-sum decomposition by transfinite recursion, splitting off injective hulls detected by associated primes. The limit-ordinal stages must remain injective and preserve the direct-sum structure; this is a structural classification task beyond routine finite module arguments.

title: Explicit Cech construction of the right adjoint for derived torsion complexes
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs the right adjoint on the unbounded derived category by an extended Cech total complex. It proves torsion of its cohomology using a filtered colimit of Koszul complexes and null homotopies, then proves the counit is invertible on the torsion subcategory. These are actual derived-category construction obligations rather than substitution into a local-cohomology formula.

title: Greenlees-May identities relating derived completion and local cohomology
difficulty_reason: Both identities are proved by constructing and filtering the two different mapping cones. The graded pieces are derived Hom from localizations or localized derived tensor products, and distinct vanishing mechanisms annihilate them. The task requires compatible control of derived completion and torsion on arbitrary complexes.

title: The image of the unit under an A-linear coherent derived equivalence is invertible
difficulty_reason: The argument first forces the image of every residue field to be concentrated in one degree by ruling out negative self-extensions. It then detects all remaining cohomology of the image of A using finite-length test modules, Nakayama, and endomorphism rings. Recovering local shifts of rank-one free modules from categorical data is a substantive reconstruction argument.

title: Amplitude, support dimension and depth of duals of finite local modules
difficulty_reason: The proof establishes three simultaneous bounds for dualizing Ext modules by induction on support dimension. The positive-depth case uses a regular element, boundary nonvanishing and support-dimension inequalities; the depth-zero case removes the finite-length torsion and reconstructs the result through a long exact sequence. The support and exact nonvanishing obligations exceed ordinary depth calculations.

title: Support and Serre S2 property of the canonical module
difficulty_reason: The support is identified using normalized localizations, the dimension function and catenarity. The S2 bound is proved by dimension induction, with separate regular-element and depth-zero torsion-removal arguments. The canonical module must satisfy two depth conditions even when the original local ring has depth zero.

title: Gorenstein ascent and descent for flat local ring homomorphisms
difficulty_reason: The proof compares residue-field Ext over the base and total rings through flat base change and a restriction right adjoint. In the descent direction it extracts the exact single-degree fibre dualizing complex after proving the base Gorenstein by faithful flatness. This controls injective dimension and the closed fibre simultaneously.

title: Gorenstein formal fibres of a local ring with a dualizing complex
difficulty_reason: The argument reduces every formal fibre to the generic fibre of a domain quotient. It then tracks the dualizing complex through completion and fraction-field localization and proves the formal-fibre dualizing object is a shift of the unit. The compatibility of completion and the generic dualizing shift is a substantive structural obligation.

title: Identification of upper shriek with derived Hom for finite ring maps
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces a general finite algebra to a monogenic quotient by a monic polynomial using transitivity. It constructs the dual basis action explicitly and shows the coefficient functional generates the algebra dual as a rank-one module. The resulting comparison identifies independently constructed derived functors, not merely their underlying complexes.

title: Expression of algebraic upper shriek by dualizing biduality
difficulty_reason: The polynomial-algebra case is proved through bounded injective models and a truncation argument valid for potentially unbounded coherent complexes. The surjection case uses a derived tensor-Hom adjunction chain and Yoneda; composition then assembles arbitrary finite-type maps. Establishing this functorial identification demands more than the existence of dualizing complexes.

title: Fibre-dimension bounds and relative Tor amplitude of a flat relative dualizing complex
difficulty_reason: Besides cohomological bounds, the proof must establish uniform Tor amplitude against arbitrary modules over the base. It uses arbitrary Noetherian base change followed by square-zero extensions to detect derived tensor with finite modules, then filtered colimits. This passage from geometric fibre bounds to all-module Tor bounds is nonroutine.

title: Existence and arbitrary base change of relative dualizing complexes for flat finitely presented algebras
difficulty_reason: The proof first descends the algebra to a finite-type integer model. For arbitrary non-Noetherian base changes it builds a relatively flat Hom model, proves universal injectivity and flatness of its successive cokernels by residue-field testing, and identifies degree-zero cohomology compatibly with the rigidifying generator. These are the core construction and base-change obligations.

title: Localization on the base of the right adjoint for proper pushforward
difficulty_reason: The proof detects a hypothetical support violation with a perfect complex, lifts that detection across the open immersion, and annihilates its adjoint map by a perfect complex on the base. The projection formula then gives a contradiction while preserving the nonzero restricted map. The actual support control of the adjoint is a nonroutine argument.

title: Tor-independent base change for the right adjoint of proper pushforward
difficulty_reason: The argument tests the canonical base-change map against a perfect generator and compares two global derived Hom complexes. It separately controls perfect and pseudo-coherent pushforward hypotheses, then proves the constructed identification is exactly the specified natural transformation through a large adjunction diagram. Identifying the map, rather than only isomorphic objects, is a core obligation.

title: Perfection, pushforward vanishing and self-duality of proper flat relative dualizing complexes
difficulty_reason: Relative perfection is detected by tensoring against every perfect object and dualizing its pushforward. The proof then establishes pushforward amplitude and reconstructs the self-Hom unit through functorial test-object identities and generation by perfect complexes. These are multiple substantive properties of an adjoint-defined complex.

title: The dualizing complex of an arbitrary projective bundle
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a candidate comparison map from the canonical top projective-bundle trace. It proves the map invertible by testing against a finite generating collection of twists and verifying the appropriate cohomology vanishing for each twist. The generator-detection argument establishes the relative dualizing object itself rather than applying Serre duality.

title: Dualizing Ext for a Koszul-regular immersion and its normal determinant
difficulty_reason: The proof explicitly identifies the dual Koszul complex with a shifted Koszul complex using contraction derivations. It tracks the odd/even sign discrepancy and the top cohomology map to the normal determinant, thereby proving both unique-degree vanishing and canonical identification. This is a structural derived calculation with compatibility obligations.

title: Compactification independence of the twisted inverse image functor
difficulty_reason: The proof compares compactifications through dense common refinements and constructs comparison maps using proper-adjoint localization. It then proves independence of the common refinement and a cocycle identity for successive refinements. The complete construction of a canonical functor is the nonroutine obligation.

title: Canonical transitivity of twisted inverse image for separated finite-type morphisms
difficulty_reason: The proof chooses compatible compactifications to construct the transitivity map, then dominates two such choices simultaneously. A five-square base-change argument establishes that the comparison agrees under these refinements. Thus the theorem proves a canonical composition law, not merely a formal adjoint identity.

title: Existence of normalized dualizing complexes on finite-type schemes
difficulty_reason: The proof inductively glues derived dualizing objects over a finite separated covering. It uses normalized uniqueness to obtain overlap identifications and then verifies compatibility of the new isomorphisms with every transition map. The substantive obligation is an effective derived gluing construction with normalization.

title: Global existence of relative dualizing complexes for flat locally finitely presented morphisms
difficulty_reason: Local algebraic relative dualizing objects are glued using uniqueness and vanishing of negative self-Ext. The argument must then separately construct the global rigidifying map on a neighbourhood of the diagonal by gluing degree-zero derived-Hom sections. Producing the object alone does not satisfy the theorem.

title: Composition of rigidified relative dualizing complexes for flat morphisms
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs the required rigidification for the tensor-product candidate through two successive diagonals. It combines exact-support derived Hom, tensor compatibility and flat base change, then repeats the construction on diagonal neighbourhoods in the nonseparated case. The rigidifying map is an actual extra construction beyond algebraic tensor transitivity.

title: Fundamental class of a local complete intersection and detection of smoothness
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a determinant map from the conormal differential sequence to the relative dualizing line. It proves that invertibility of this map forces the maximal-rank Jacobian condition for a local complete-intersection presentation. Both the fundamental class construction and the converse smoothness criterion are substantive obligations.

title: Deligne systems represent derived Hom after restriction to an open subscheme
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces to Ext of coherent sheaves, then proves both injectivity and surjectivity by induction on Ext degree. Artin-Rees controls the changing kernels and powers of the boundary ideal while coherent extensions kill and lift extension classes. The pro-system comparison is a long exactness-and-lifting argument.

title: Topological duality between coherent cohomology and compactly supported cohomology
difficulty_reason: The proof extends a coherent complex to a compactification and represents ordinary cohomology as a colimit of boundary-ideal Ext groups. Derived bidual evaluation and proper duality convert this into an inverse-limit model for compact support. The limit/colimit passage produces the asserted topological vector-space duality.

title: Nonvanishing of top coherent cohomology forces a variety to be proper
difficulty_reason: The proof compactifies the variety and converts top cohomology into compactly supported cohomology of its dual. It proves the relevant lowest dual cohomology sheaf is torsion-free and consequently has no section supported away from a nonempty boundary. This is the key duality-and-support vanishing argument establishing properness.

title: Equidimensionality of catenary Noetherian local S2 rings
difficulty_reason: The proof separates maximal-dimensional from lower-dimensional irreducible components and chooses a generic intersection point. Catenarity forces a local dimension at least two, while S2 forces depth at least two; the resulting punctured spectrum is disconnected, contradicting depth-two connectedness. The geometric contradiction is more than a routine dimension formula.

title: Local-to-global finiteness of low local-cohomology modules
difficulty_reason: The proof removes zero-degree torsion and inducts using a regular element. It proves finiteness of the associated-prime set of the potentially nonfinite local-cohomology modules, then assembles local annihilator exponents into a uniform global exponent. This is a genuine finiteness theorem, not ordinary localization of a finite module.

title: Associated-point criterion for coherence of pushforward from an open subscheme
difficulty_reason: The proof inducts simultaneously on associated points and generic-stalk length, extending local maps by multiplying by functions. The reverse direction constructs an injection from an integral support sheaf using its associated point. These two constructions reduce coherence of an arbitrary coherent sheaf to its associated integral components.

title: Coherence across codimension-two boundaries on Nagata universally catenary schemes
difficulty_reason: The proof normalizes the integral supports at associated points and uses finiteness of normalization. It then proves depth at least two along the boundary using normality and the dimension formula, so that the normalized coherent sheaf satisfies a Hartogs extension theorem. The normalization-and-depth construction is the nonroutine content.

title: Descent of etale sheaf sections along submersive morphisms with connected geometric fibres
difficulty_reason: One must turn equality of stalk values into equality on entire geometric fibres, using connectedness of the pulled-back constant sheaf. The saturated maximal equality locus must then descend to an open subset through submersiveness, allowing local sections to glue globally.

title: Reconstruction of affine scheme morphisms from locally ringed etale topoi
difficulty_reason: Recovering the ring map on global sections is only the first step: the proof must identify the inverse-image functor on every affine etale representable. Polynomial equalizer presentations and local maps of strictly henselian stalks produce these identifications, whose functoriality and compatibility with structure sheaves must be verified.

title: Full faithfulness of etale base change under universal homeomorphisms
difficulty_reason: The problem requires constructing the unique descent isomorphism over the double fibre product, where the diagonal is a thickening. One must also prove the cocycle condition via the triple fibre product and show naturality, turning the forgetful descent-data functor into an equivalence.

title: Higher direct images commute with inverse limits of quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme morphisms
difficulty_reason: The comparison map must be constructed coherently for varying source and target schemes and varying coefficient sheaves. Beyond continuity of cohomology on affine etale objects, the proof must identify the sheafified colimit and establish local injectivity and surjectivity, or alternatively perform dimension shifting in the category of sheaf systems.

title: Cohomological descent and its spectral sequence for surjective finite scheme morphisms
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs the augmented cosimplicial sheaf complex attached to the entire Cech nerve of a finite surjection. Exactness must be proved on geometric stalks by identifying the nerve with powers of a finite nonempty fibre, then finite pushforward acyclicity must be used to obtain the asserted descent spectral sequence.

title: Every etale structure-sheaf module on a zero-dimensional local scheme is quasi-coherent
difficulty_reason: An arbitrary module sheaf must be reconstructed from global sections, not merely checked on a given affine presentation. The proof reduces every etale object to finite local etale algebras and uses semilinear Galois descent twice to handle both Galois and non-Galois residue extensions.

title: The Brauer class of a degree-d Azumaya algebra is annihilated by d
difficulty_reason: The proof must construct a canonical antisymmetrization section in the d-fold tensor power that glues despite line-bundle ambiguity in local splitting modules. Its right ideal gives a globally defined splitting module of the precise rank, yielding an endomorphism-algebra description without assuming d! is invertible.

title: Finite-dimensional top coherent cohomology of separated finite-type schemes over a field
difficulty_reason: The statement does not assume properness, so standard proper cohomology finiteness cannot be applied directly. The proof combines induction on dimension and coherent devissage with Chow modification, relative ampleness and a lower-dimensional cokernel, then obtains a surjection from cohomology on a projective compactification.

title: Tsen-Lang theorem for function fields of r-dimensional varieties over algebraically closed fields
difficulty_reason: The central task is to construct a nonzero common solution by replacing rational unknowns with global sections of increasing ample powers. Asymptotic Riemann-Roch must compare the growth of the coefficient equations and unknown sections with the sharp inequality n>d^r, reducing the problem to homogeneous intersection over an algebraically closed field.

title: Finite representable coequalizer presentations of constructible etale sheaves
difficulty_reason: A finite stratification alone does not furnish a global presentation by etale representables. The proof must extend stalk elements from the closed stratum to ambient etale neighbourhoods, use quasi-compactness to make finitely many lifts suffice, and inductively combine this with the open strata; the kernel relation then supplies the coequalizer.

title: Global section rigidity for spectral spaces with connected specialization intersections
difficulty_reason: Surjectivity of restriction for arbitrary sheaves must be proved from connected intersections with closures of points. The proof reduces via filtered constructible presentations and embeddings into finite closed-supported constant sheaves, while proving that global membership in a subsheaf is detected on the closed subset.

title: Vanishing, finiteness, and algebraically closed base change for torsion etale cohomology of curves
difficulty_reason: Arbitrary torsion coefficients must be reduced to constructible prime-field local systems without losing any of eight conclusions. The proof performs prime-power devissage and separates a dense open into irreducible components, then uses extension by zero to assemble the curve statements from the established local-system case.

title: Proper base change for arbitrary torsion etale coefficients
difficulty_reason: After a nontrivial reduction to the projective line, one must compute cohomology over a strictly henselian local base using restricted injective resolutions. The proof compares the resulting stalks with closed-fibre cohomology and checks arbitrary field extensions, then promotes prime coefficients to all torsion via the injective criterion.

title: Relative cohomological-dimension bound twice the fibre dimension for proper morphisms
difficulty_reason: The proof must control arbitrary torsion sheaves by dimension induction, including singular and nonnormal schemes. Normalization produces a lower-dimensional cokernel, while the graph of a rational map to the projective line produces a derived error supported in codimension at least two; Leray then gives the sharp twice-dimension bound.

title: Affine etale cohomological dimension is bounded by dimension plus the field cohomological dimension
difficulty_reason: Noether normalization alone does not give the desired bound: the proof needs local strict-henselian estimates indexed by residue transcendence degree. Two support estimates control the boundary of a partial compactification, and a careful two-stage Leray analysis bounds every diagonal of the spectral sequence.

title: Product base change for open immersions with invertible torsion coefficients
difficulty_reason: The proof must handle an arbitrary nonsmooth product factor, so smooth base change alone is insufficient. A minimal-dimensional counterexample is forced onto closed points by strict-henselian dimension reduction; projective compactification and the one-proper-factor Kunneth formula then annihilate its cone.

title: Universal punctual base change for etale cohomology over a field
difficulty_reason: The result treats arbitrary schemes over the field and arbitrary quasi-compact quasi-separated test morphisms. The proof approximates the scheme and coefficients, reduces hypothetical failures to algebraically closed fraction fields, then builds a directed system of finite-type opens to recover base change from the open-immersion product theorem.

title: Unbounded quasi-coherent complexes satisfy affine fppf cohomological descent
difficulty_reason: The bounded-below comparison does not automatically apply to arbitrary unbounded complexes. The proof must reconstruct the sheaf complex as a derived inverse limit of truncations using eventual stabilization on every affine object, and justify passing derived global sections through that inverse limit.

title: Beck monadicity
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a quasi-inverse to the comparison functor using split coequalizers and proves the required natural isomorphisms. This reconstructs an entire category of algebras; it is not a routine verification of a given adjunction.

title: Morita equivalence classification
difficulty_reason: The proof reconstructs bimodules implementing an equivalence and proves evaluation and coevaluation are isomorphisms from the finite projective generator hypotheses. The core Morita equivalence is proved rather than assumed; Eilenberg-Watts is recorded prerequisite material.

title: Gabriel compact-projective-generator theorem
difficulty_reason: The proof reconstructs arbitrary modules from presentations using a compact projective generator, and proves fullness and essential surjectivity of the Hom functor. This category reconstruction exceeds routine calculations with projective modules.

title: Classification of Galois categories by finite continuous automorphism-group sets
difficulty_reason: The axioms must produce both full faithfulness and essential surjectivity rather than assume the category already comes from a profinite group. The proof realizes equivariant maps as graphs of connected components and constructs every coset object by a quotient of a Galois object whose stabilizer lies in the prescribed open subgroup.

title: Finite etale covers of proper schemes over henselian local rings are determined by the closed fibre
difficulty_reason: One must algebraize the entire compatible infinitesimal tower of a finite etale cover and establish full faithfulness through graph lifting. The proof then uses approximation of solutions over the completion and a directed-limit reduction through henselian Noetherian G-rings to handle an arbitrary henselian local base.

title: Fundamental-group exact sequence for a punctured local spectrum and its strict henselization
difficulty_reason: A cover trivialized over the strictly henselian punctured spectrum must extend over the original local spectrum. The proof analyzes the double and triple strict-henselian fibre products to extend the descent isomorphism and its cocycle across the missing closed points, then applies effective affine descent.

title: Etaleness of inertia invariants for finite group actions on arbitrary rings
difficulty_reason: The proof must show the invariant-ring map is etale at a selected prime without normality or finite-type assumptions. Etale localization splits the integral fibre, and a further equivariant clopen refinement makes the group permute factors; the inertia subgroup then identifies a factor of the full invariant ring.

title: Arithmetic fundamental-group exact sequence for geometrically connected schemes over a field
difficulty_reason: One must establish geometric-kernel normality and injectivity as well as surjectivity to the absolute Galois group. The proof descends the Galois orbit of a split component, approximates arbitrary geometric finite etale covers over finite field extensions, and proves the exact-kernel criterion by descending a complete splitting.

title: Homotopy exact sequence for proper flat families with geometrically connected reduced fibres
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs an adjoint to pullback on finite etale covers using Stein factorization, rather than merely applying abstract exactness. A cover with one trivial geometric fibre component must be shown to equal the pullback of its Stein factor by a degree-one argument on a connected scheme.

title: Stability of exact complexes under Artin-Rees controlled perturbation
difficulty_reason: The proof iteratively corrects a vector by the perturbed image while raising its I-adic order and preserving its image. It then proves a uniform Artin-Rees bound for the perturbed map and closes exactness using Krull intersection; these quantitative coupled corrections exceed a routine application of Artin-Rees.

title: Patching equivalence for flat modules over a fibre product
difficulty_reason: The central obligation is to prove flatness of the patched fibre-product module for arbitrary ideals. The author reduces through the kernel ideal, proves Tor vanishing, saturates an ideal as an A-prime-module and recovers injectivity; the equivalence follows only after this substantive tensor argument.

title: Principal Fitting ideals and projective-dimension-one decomposition
difficulty_reason: The author must extract a free summand and identify the torsion part from two Fitting conditions. A nonzerodivisor minor and adjugate-type matrix argument prove that the relation image is finite free, after which local splitting globalizes; this carries real structure and homological-dimension work.

title: Etale-local lifting of sections of smooth algebras
difficulty_reason: The proof stabilizes a projective conormal module to a free one by adjoining a symmetric algebra. It chooses equations, verifies vanishing of the cotangent obstruction and differentials, and localizes the resulting algebra to construct an etale lift with the prescribed closed-fibre section.

title: Construction and universal property of henselization of pairs
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs henselization as a directed colimit of etale neighbourhoods and explicitly verifies directedness, the residue quotient, and the henselian property. Its adjunction requires coherent uniqueness of sections proved by diagonal idempotents; existence is not delegated to a pre-existing henselization theorem.

title: Finiteness of the next Serre-depth defect locus
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces the next-depth defect to the preceding Serre level along a carefully chosen regular element. It then chooses that element so its complement lies entirely in the Cohen-Macaulay locus, leaving only the finitely many induction defects. This is a global finiteness argument for a depth-stratified locus.

title: Faltings annihilator theorem for local cohomology
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a global annihilator by a double induction on cohomological degree and dimension-function strata. Spectral-sequence filtrations control successive powers of annihilators, and finite dualizing Ext supports produce uniform choices. The converse locates a minimal failing depth-codimension pair and proves its local cohomology cannot be annihilated.

title: Completion inequalities for the depth-codimension finiteness cutoff
difficulty_reason: The proof tracks chains of primes across completion and splits all dimension terms into base and formal-fibre contributions. It constructs minimal lifts for one inequality, then handles the competing formal-fibre dimensions using the Serre bound and a separate large-fibre case. The minimization is not preserved by a routine faithful-flatness argument.

title: Hartshorne-Lichtenbaum top local-cohomology vanishing
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces through completion and maximal-dimensional components to a complete local domain. It then replaces the support ideal by a one-dimensional prime and changes ordinary powers to symbolic powers in a dualizing Ext colimit; the depth of these symbolic quotients forces vanishing. The task requires the duality-and-symbolic-power mechanism rather than ordinary cohomological dimension bounds.

title: Injectivity of residue-supported modules with characteristic-zero derivation operators
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a socle-preserving embedding into a sum of injective hulls. Leibniz operators force divisibility by a parameter, and an induction on dimension then proves surjectivity on parameter torsion. This is a module classification from differential-operator structure with a complete divisibility argument.

title: Injectivity of residue-supported Frobenius-stable modules over regular local rings
difficulty_reason: The proof computes all Frobenius-power torsion layers using flatness of iterated Frobenius and shows these layers are free over truncated parameter quotients. It obtains parameter divisibility, then verifies Frobenius stability passes to parameter torsion and inducts on dimension. This is a distinct positive-characteristic classification task, not a parameter change of the derivation proof.

title: Uniform annihilation of high Tor against every ideal-power quotient
difficulty_reason: The proof represents derived tensor with ideal powers as cohomology on the blowup. A bounded spectral sequence assembles sheafwise annihilators into a uniform global exponent, independent of the module, homological degree and power of the ideal. The uniformity and filtration control remain substantive after the local blowup estimates.

title: Verdier multiplicative systems associated to triangulated subcategories
difficulty_reason: The proof verifies the Ore and triangle-compatibility conditions using octahedra and the nine-triangle construction. The converse saturation implication requires an additional cone diagram, a zero composite and splitting to recover the individual cones. This establishes the localization machinery and the precise relation between saturation of arrows and subcategories.

title: Essential surjectivity of the derived functor to a Serre quotient
difficulty_reason: The proof strictifies a complex in the quotient category in both directions: pushouts handle nonnegative degrees and pullbacks handle negative degrees. It must then replace terms by finite sums of images and intersections of kernels so the lifted differentials square to zero in the original category. This is an actual lifting construction for unbounded quotient complexes.

title: Existence of unbounded left derived functors under exact sequential colimits
difficulty_reason: The proof builds a compatible sequence of bounded-above resolutions whose colimit resolves an arbitrary complex. It handles the essential difficulty that a morphism of colimit resolutions need not come from levelwise maps, using common bounded resolutions and compatible cohomology comparisons. Exactness and preservation of sequential colimits then yield the desired quasi-isomorphism.

title: K-injective limits of truncation resolutions and derived completeness
difficulty_reason: The proof builds the ordinary inverse limit of split-surjective injective resolutions degree by degree. It constructs a termwise split product exact sequence proving that this limit is both K-injective and the derived truncation limit, then identifies the canonical comparison from the original complex. The criterion exposes precisely the obstruction to using truncation resolutions in the unbounded category.

title: Existence and isomorphism of Postnikov systems under Hom vanishing
difficulty_reason: The proof inductively extends a totalization tower and identifies its obstruction as a composite into an earlier cone. Iterated distinguished triangles and the shifted Hom bounds annihilate that obstruction; the stronger bounds then lift the identity to an isomorphism of systems. This is an obstruction-theoretic existence theorem for totalizing complexes in abstract triangulated categories.

title: Finite etale covers of normal punctured spectra are equivalent to finite normal algebras
difficulty_reason: The global sections of a finite etale cover must be proved finite over the local base, despite the punctured spectrum being nonaffine. The proof identifies these sections with an integral closure by localizing along the puncture and using reflexivity and depth-two Hartogs extension, thereby constructing the inverse equivalence.

title: Purity of finite etale covers of regular local punctured spectra
difficulty_reason: The dimension-two case requires proving flatness of a finite normal algebra through Cohen-Macaulay structure and then excluding a zero-dimensional branch locus by the discriminant. In higher dimension one must reduce covers across a regular parameter while retaining the extension property, completing a nontrivial dimension induction.

title: Unique reflexive finite extension of etale covers across depth-two complements
difficulty_reason: The proof must extend a finite etale algebra to a coherent reflexive algebra and prove uniqueness among finite depth-two extensions. It also identifies etaleness with flatness using codimension-one ramification control and establishes flat-base-change compatibility of the extension construction.

title: Effective exceptional canonical divisors characterize rational surface singularities
difficulty_reason: The proof must convert an effective exceptional canonical divisor into equality of derived pushforwards. Trace and Grauert-Riemenschneider vanishing are combined with a depth-two isomorphism argument, and duality then gives rationality; minimality additionally forces the exceptional divisor to vanish.

title: Purity of the ramification locus for finite-type maps from normal schemes to regular schemes
difficulty_reason: Unlike purity for already quasi-finite maps, this statement must first force quasi-finiteness from codimension-one etaleness. The proof uses completion and normalized hypersurface sections to show that the exceptional fibre point is closed, then reduces the remaining ramification to branch-locus purity.

title: Affineness of the maximal etale locus over excellent regular schemes
difficulty_reason: The proof must show the etale locus is affine even when its complement is not a divisor. It localizes over the regular target, uses purity and Hartshorne-Lichtenbaum vanishing to bound the structure-sheaf cohomological dimension of the locus, then applies the prior local affineness criterion to finish the dimension induction.

title: Characteristic-p coordinate modification decreases the nonfinite invariant of an etale algebra lift
difficulty_reason: The construction must make an additional generator integral while preserving etaleness and the prescribed quotient map. It chooses a polynomial relation and adds carefully chosen p-power terms to the coordinates, controlling integrality, Kähler differentials and the kernel ideal simultaneously to force strict descent of the invariant.

title: Existence of relative divided power envelopes for arbitrary ring-ideal maps
difficulty_reason: Representability requires a solution-set construction, not simply a formal appeal to a free polynomial algebra. The proof constructs a bounded divided-power subalgebra containing all specified images and operations, then verifies compatibility with arbitrary limits to produce the universal envelope.

title: Divided power envelopes commute with Tor-controlled flat base change
difficulty_reason: The proof must extend divided powers through a possibly nonflat algebra base change. A polynomial presentation and the Tor hypothesis identify the relation ideal intersection, while flatness modulo the original divided power ideal proves an auxiliary injection that allows divided powers to descend through the quotient.

title: Every crystalline module crystal carries a canonical integrable connection
difficulty_reason: The connection must be constructed functorially from the crystal isomorphisms on a first-order divided-power thickening. Integrability is a separate substantive obligation: the cocycle identity on a specifically constructed second-order thickening must be expanded and identified with the curvature in the exterior square.

title: Crystals on affine crystalline sites yield complete modules with topologically quasi-nilpotent integrable connections
difficulty_reason: Beyond extracting a connection, the proof must reconstruct a complete module from its reductions and prove topological quasi-nilpotence. It expands the crystal transport in divided-power diagonal coordinates and uses the triple-diagonal cocycle to identify every coefficient with iterated commuting connection operators, forcing p-adic decay.

title: Crystalline cohomology of affine crystals is computed by the completed divided-power de Rham complex
difficulty_reason: The proof must identify the crystal Cech resolution with a de Rham complex through a two-directional double-complex argument. It uses relative divided-power Poincare comparison for every row and verifies that all coprojection identifications agree on cohomology, producing the alternating zero/identity differentials and canonical comparison.

title: A p-power divided-power extension admits a de Rham homotopy inverse up to multiplication by p
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs an explicit p-adically continuous integration operator on a divided-power basis for a pth-root extension. Its recursion must simultaneously control denominators, identify differential splitting and universal injectivity, and establish the factor and horizontality identities before the homotopy-inverse criterion applies.

title: Finite etale algebras over a henselian pair
difficulty_reason: Full faithfulness is proved by identifying algebra maps with sections and then with lifted idempotents. Essential surjectivity uses integral closure, decomposition of the closed fibre, and localization to produce a finite etale lift, so an entire equivalence must be constructed.

title: Descent of projectivity through finite injective ring extensions
difficulty_reason: The proof changes to a faithfully flat finite locally free extension where the integral algebra splits into polynomial-root pieces. It patches projectivity across quotient ideals, controls the nilpotent intersection, and combines descended flatness with lifting of projectives; the extension is not assumed flat.

title: Reflexive modules and codimension-one intersections
difficulty_reason: The key direction expresses the codimension-one intersection inside the generic fibre as a kernel with a direct-sum target. Localizing this description and using depth at higher-codimension primes proves equality with the original module, after which DVR reflexivity identifies the double dual.

title: Blowing up a finite module to make its strict transform locally free
difficulty_reason: The author reduces a finite module to a finitely presented approximation without losing its strict transform. A Fitting ideal supplies the blowup centre, and nonzerodivisor control of relations proves local freeness of every specified transform; the centre is explicitly constructed.

title: Universal injectivity of a completed direct sum into a product
difficulty_reason: The proof describes completion by coordinate families that converge I-adically, but ordinary injectivity is insufficient. Uniform Artin-Rees bounds lift each relation while preserving convergence, proving injectivity after tensoring with every finite module.

title: First Koszul homology regularity implies quasi-regularity
difficulty_reason: The proof first controls coefficients of pure powers using vanishing of first Koszul homology. A faithfully flat polynomial extension and a generic change of basis reduce all homogeneous coefficient relations to that special case, yielding the associated-graded conclusion.

title: Independence of polynomial presentation for Koszul-regular kernels
difficulty_reason: The author constructs a common polynomial presentation and compares conormal dimensions of its two kernels. Local bases, concatenation of regular sequences, and a change-of-generators argument transfer Koszul regularity to the other presentation rather than assuming presentation independence.

title: Continuous lifting through closed topologically nilpotent ideals
difficulty_reason: The author constructs a compatible two-parameter grid of lifts through square-zero fibre-product surjections. A diagonal inverse limit produces the lift, and a quantitative power estimate proves continuity; ordinary formal smoothness alone does not directly supply these compatible topological lifts.

title: Testing formal smoothness by small Artinian extensions
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces arbitrary lifting diagrams to local Artinian ones with the same residue field. For square-zero kernels of arbitrary dimension it forms a product of one-dimensional quotient extensions and splits the resulting vector-space kernel to recover a lift.

title: Filtered subfield intersections and characteristic-p differentials
difficulty_reason: The author detects a differential relation through a p-basis and uses directed subfield intersections to force its coefficients into pth powers. For finite field extensions it reduces through a tower to separable and purely inseparable primitive cases and proves compatibility of the intersection.

title: A derivation detecting a non-pth-power in a finite-type domain
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces by normalization and denominator scaling to a finite algebra over a power-series polynomial ring. A carefully chosen finite-index subfield preserves the nonzero differential, allowing a fraction-field derivation to be scaled back to the domain without killing the chosen element.

title: Regularity of flat complete local maps with geometrically regular closed fibre
difficulty_reason: The author must prove geometric regularity at every prime, not just at the closed fibre. It reduces to a power-series base and inducts through purely inseparable extensions, extending derivations to detect each degree-p equation and preserve regularity.

title: Henselization preserves the G-ring property
difficulty_reason: The proof compares individual completed formal fibres with products of henselization fibres. It handles strict henselization separately through a formally smooth completion map and separable residue-field extensions, tracking the base field of geometric regularity throughout.

title: Essentially finite-type algebras over G-rings remain G-rings
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces arbitrary finite-type algebras to one polynomial variable and compares local completions by a two-step square. It reduces formal fibres to a regular complete local domain and separates positive-characteristic prime cases, retaining the geometric-regularity obligation.

title: Nagata local rings and geometrically reduced formal fibres
difficulty_reason: One direction uses finite local domain extensions and analytic unramifiedness to control formal fibres. The reverse direction constructs a finite integral model inside an arbitrary finite residue-field extension and identifies its completed localization, so all geometric field extensions are addressed.

title: Restriction of scalars detects pseudo-coherence
difficulty_reason: The difficult direction builds a finite free approximation after extending scalars and lowers the highest nonzero cohomology degree by a cone. It proves that the cone preserves pseudo-coherence over the base and inductively recovers a finite approximation over the target algebra.

title: Lifting a prescribed projective complex across an ideal
difficulty_reason: The author lifts an acyclic mapping cone and then constructs a comparison map whose degreewise cokernels stay in the chosen projective class. A separate split-injectivity argument removes the remaining obstruction, producing a complex that simultaneously represents the original derived object and has the prescribed reduction.

title: Perfect complexes are exactly compact derived objects
difficulty_reason: The converse uses compactness first to bound cohomology and then to factor the identity through a bounded free complex. A degree-by-degree finite-support induction turns that complex into a finite free one, and a split idempotent identifies the original object as a perfect summand.

title: Gluing perfectness across two quotient ideals
difficulty_reason: After removing a square-zero quotient the proof realizes the object in a fibre-product exact sequence of K-flat complexes. It proves compactness through derived Hom comparisons over the three quotients and a five-lemma argument, recovering perfectness over the product ideal.

title: Strong generation by the ring forces finite-dimensional regularity
difficulty_reason: The proof realizes a universal Ext class by a truncated finite free resolution and factors it through a sequence of cohomologically zero maps. The ghost lemma annihilates the composite, forcing a uniform projective-dimension bound for all finite modules and hence finite-dimensional regularity.

title: Kunz flat-Frobenius criterion for regularity
difficulty_reason: The converse transports independence of minimal generators through the flat Frobenius map. It computes the length of the Frobenius parameter quotient and compares the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial at scaled powers to force embedding dimension equal to dimension. The length asymptotics and independence argument are the decisive nonroutine obligations.

title: Uniform twist vanishing for almost-projective modules on a blowup
difficulty_reason: The proof splits the failure of pullback exactness into two coherent short exact sequences with error supported on a controlled exceptional thickening. Descending induction on cohomological degree builds explicit twist shifts that annihilate transition maps, and a separate boundary-map argument controls degree-zero images. The constants depend on the associated graded ring and error thickness, so ordinary Serre vanishing does not establish the conclusion.

title: The nine-triangle diagram in a triangulated category
difficulty_reason: The proof applies the octahedral axiom three times to construct all rows and columns. It then checks the factorization identities controlling the central squares and the required anticommutativity at the lower-right corner. This is a substantial sign-sensitive existence theorem from the abstract triangulated axioms.

title: Existence of strict filtered-injective resolutions of bounded-below filtered complexes
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs compatible resolutions of each kernel and coimage, combines them through split exact sequences, and builds a double complex with square-zero horizontal differential. It then proves its totalization is a filtered quasi-isomorphism by comparing associated graded total complexes. Resolving the exact filtered category requires these additional compatibility constructions.

title: Unbounded right derived functors with finite cohomological dimension
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs acyclic-term replacements for arbitrary unbounded complexes and proves the resulting functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Truncation cones and a hypercohomology spectral sequence isolate a finite cohomological window, after which separate distinguished-triangle arguments establish the sharp truncation and amplitude bounds. The unbounded case cannot be settled by ordinary bounded injective resolutions.

title: Finite-stage descent of flatness along a filtered colimit
difficulty_reason: The proof extracts finitely many principal opens covering the relevant closed subset of the limit spectrum. It descends both a unit-ideal equation and local flatness to one common finite stage, then extends the argument from finite presentation to essential finite presentation.

title: Quasi-coherence and uniform universal vanishing of higher direct images for qcqs morphisms
difficulty_reason: The proof must handle nonseparated sources by gluing higher direct images through relative Mayer-Vietoris, not just compute one affine-cover Cech complex. It also constructs a cohomological-degree bound from finite covers and all their intersections that remains valid after every base change.

title: Flat base change for quasi-coherent cohomology of arbitrary qcqs schemes
difficulty_reason: The separated Cech calculation is insufficient for arbitrary quasi-separated schemes. The proof must compare the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequences after base change, use the separated comparison on every overlap, and identify the resulting canonical comparison with the higher-direct-image base-change map.

title: Flat coefficient base change and projection for higher quasi-coherent direct images
difficulty_reason: The comparison must be constructed globally from derived adjunction and cup products even though the base-change morphism itself is not assumed flat. A finite-in-each-degree affine hypercovering is then needed to prove the isomorphism using flatness of the coefficient module over the original base.

title: Extension of coherent sheaf morphisms after modifying their domain off an open subset
difficulty_reason: The proof must globalize extension from a Noetherian local region to a merely locally Noetherian scheme. It constructs a partially ordered system of compatible coherent domain subsheaves and extended maps, proves gluing along chains, and uses local extension to rule out a proper maximal domain.

title: Coherent sheaves admit filtrations by ideal sheaves on integral closed subschemes
difficulty_reason: The proof must reduce arbitrary coherent sheaves, including nonreduced support, to rank-one ideal objects on integral closed subschemes. It combines minimal-support induction, splitting reducible support, ideal-power devissage and a generic-rank embedding with a smaller-support cokernel.

title: Affineness descends under finite surjective morphisms to Noetherian schemes
difficulty_reason: The finite cover need not be flat, so ordinary faithfully flat descent of affineness does not apply. The proof constructs coherent test sheaves above integral support strata and verifies cohomological devissage for all their ideal modifications, forcing H1 vanishing on the target.

title: Serre finiteness, twisting vanishing and graded-section finiteness on projective space
difficulty_reason: The problem must prove finiteness and eventual vanishing for arbitrary coherent sheaves, not simply compute the twists of the structure sheaf. A descending cohomological induction through finite sums of twists establishes both properties together, then graded tail comparison controls all section degrees.

title: Ampleness descends through finite surjective maps of proper Noetherian schemes
difficulty_reason: The difficult implication cannot assume the finite surjection is flat or use section norms directly. The proof builds a cohomological property of twisted coherent sheaves and verifies generic-support devissage by finite pushforward, projection and higher-cohomology vanishing on the covering scheme.

title: Ampleness is invariant under Noetherian nilpotent thickenings
difficulty_reason: Sections giving affine opens on the reduced closed subscheme need not lift, and the proof must remove the H1 obstruction. After reduction to square-zero ideals, the connecting map is treated as a derivation, so powers of a section kill its obstruction and produce affine principal opens on the thickening.

title: Proper pushforward preserves coherent cohomology over locally Noetherian bases
difficulty_reason: The proof must reduce arbitrary coherent modules to suitable generically rank-one sheaves whose direct images are controlled. A Chow modification and a twist ample for two maps create such test objects with vanishing higher direct images, and relative Leray plus coherent devissage complete the finiteness argument.

title: Ideal-power cohomology and ideal powers of cohomology are pro-isomorphic under properness
difficulty_reason: The proof must control kernels and transition images uniformly, not merely compare completed limits. Finite graded Rees-module generation and generation of its kernel module yield shifted transition bounds, allowing explicit reverse maps and verification of both pro-system compositions.

title: Fibrewise ampleness yields uniform local twisted-cohomology vanishing and section lifting
difficulty_reason: One must obtain a single twist bound across every infinitesimal thickening of the fibre. The proof packages the layers as a finite graded module over the associated graded base algebra, then combines exact-sequence induction, formal functions and Nakayama to transfer vanishing and section surjectivity back to the local base.

title: Proper flat coherent cohomology is perfect and obeys arbitrary derived base change
difficulty_reason: Flat base change alone does not cover an arbitrary base algebra and does not prove perfectness. The proof replaces the Cech resolution by its bounded alternating complex, proves flatness termwise, and uses square-zero base algebras to detect uniform Tor amplitude before deducing perfectness from pseudo-coherence.

title: Algebraization of coherent formal systems on projective schemes over complete Noetherian rings
difficulty_reason: Essential surjectivity requires constructing a coherent algebraic presentation for a compatible formal system. Uniform twisting vanishing lifts finitely many generators through every infinitesimal level, producing a surjection from a completed finite sum of ample twists; a second presentation and full faithfulness then algebraize the cokernel.

title: Grothendieck algebraization of proper formal schemes with a compatible ample line bundle
difficulty_reason: The proof must simultaneously lift a projective embedding through all infinitesimal levels with a uniform choice of degree. It builds a finite graded algebra from successive ideal layers, uses uniform H1 vanishing to lift the embedding sections, and algebraizes the resulting compatible system of closed projective subschemes.

title: Uniform derived cohomological-dimension bounds for unbounded quasi-coherent complexes
difficulty_reason: Finite cohomological dimension on individual sheaves must be promoted to truncation control for unbounded complexes. The proof computes the derived inverse limit of lower truncations, proves eventual stabilization in each degree and kills the lim1 term, thereby obtaining explicit degree bounds.

title: Local derived pushforward compatibility implies global quasi-coherent derived-category equivalence
difficulty_reason: The unit and counit of the derived coherator must be proved invertible for every unbounded object. The proof inducts on the number of affine opens meeting the closed support, constructs localization triangles and uses coherator-pushforward compatibility to reduce both maps to the affine case.

title: Derived quasi-coherent pushforward agrees with sheaf-theoretic pushforward on affine-diagonal schemes
difficulty_reason: The comparison is not a formal consequence of the underived equality because the two ambient categories have different resolutions. The proof identifies suitable pushed-forward K-injectives and then uses two kernel/image/cokernel sequences to induct on support and extend the comparison to arbitrary complexes.

title: Finite-level pseudo-coherence descends under fppf coverings
difficulty_reason: Descent of cohomology modules alone does not produce a finite-level complex resolution. The proof reduces the cover to one flat affine finite-presentation cover, lifts top-degree generators to a map from a shifted finite free sheaf, and inducts through its cone while retaining the precise pseudo-coherence bound.

title: Closed immersion pushforward detects finite-level pseudo-coherence
difficulty_reason: The equivalence requires constructive local finite presentations in both directions under only pseudo-coherence of the ambient structure module. The proof uses adjunction to lift top-degree generators, compares their cones after exact pushforward and performs two separate inductions controlling the pseudo-coherence level.

title: Perfect complexes on affine opens extend stably by a shifted vector bundle
difficulty_reason: A perfect complex on a quasi-compact open need not extend directly, so the proof must identify the precise stable correction. It truncates a global pseudo-coherent lift far below its Tor amplitude, proves the resulting syzygy is a vector bundle and uses uniform Ext vanishing to split the correction triangle.

title: Perfect approximation glues across an affine open and a quasi-compact open
difficulty_reason: The proof must glue approximating complexes and their maps, not merely their cohomology modules. A stabilized perfect complex is extended across the overlap with support, its map is modified to lift, and derived gluing plus cone induction constructs the required globally supported approximation.

title: Pseudo-coherent complexes are controlled homotopy colimits of perfect approximations
difficulty_reason: Independent approximations do not automatically form a compatible directed system. The proof uses degree-specific Ext vanishing to factor each previously chosen perfect approximation through the next, then verifies truncation stabilization and the homotopy-colimit comparison.

title: Relative Ext with proper flat coherent coefficients is represented by pseudo-coherent complexes
difficulty_reason: The proof must represent all coefficient-variable Ext functors, not only each fixed Ext group. Perfect approximations give finite-degree representing complexes; their duals must then be assembled into a homotopy colimit with controlled truncations to obtain one pseudo-coherent object representing every degree and its boundary maps.

title: Perfect derived complexes descend through directed inverse limits of qcqs schemes
difficulty_reason: Finite presentation handles individual affine complexes but does not supply global descent of their derived gluing data. The proof descends complexes on two open pieces, descends their overlap isomorphism, and uses a map to derived pushforward to glue an object whose derived pullback is the original perfect complex.

title: Derived Stein splitting near geometrically reduced fibres of proper flat families
difficulty_reason: The proof must split the zero-degree piece of derived pushforward while ensuring the remaining piece has positive Tor amplitude. It proves fibrewise section surjectivity by passing to an algebraically closed residue field and lifting fibre idempotents, then identifies the zero-degree algebra as finite etale on a neighbourhood.

title: A finite family of boundary ideals detects the resolution property
difficulty_reason: The proof must replace the requirement to resolve every finite-type quasi-coherent sheaf by finitely many specified ideal quotients. It descends the boundary ideals and vector bundles to a Noetherian model, then extends generators across boundary ideal powers and uses tensor powers of the chosen bundles to resolve an arbitrary coherent sheaf.

title: Nisnevich induction principle for quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces
difficulty_reason: An algebraic space cannot be covered by affine Zariski opens, so the scheme induction principle does not suffice. The proof uses a finite scheme-stratified etale filtration and refines each stage into elementary distinguished squares with affine chart, showing that all overlap objects meet the inductive hypotheses.

title: Derived objects and compatible morphisms glue across elementary distinguished squares
difficulty_reason: The proof must glue derived objects from a Zariski open and an etale neighbourhood that need not be an open subspace. It builds a derived fibre triangle, then uses support on the closed complement and conservativity of etale pushforward there to prove the second restriction isomorphism and the compatible-map statement.

title: Derived quasi-coherent comparison equivalence from affine etale pushforward compatibility
difficulty_reason: The algebraic-space proof requires more than the scheme support induction: it must lift arbitrary derived morphisms to actual maps after suitable quasi-isomorphisms and control their null homotopies. It proves both fullness and faithfulness using supported cones, then establishes essential surjectivity by an adjunction argument detecting vanishing on every affine etale chart.

title: Finite polynomial simplicial resolutions of finite-type algebras
difficulty_reason: The proof inductively replaces a coskeletal resolution in its next degree by a finite polynomial algebra. It must preserve the trivial Kan fibration through the replacement and prove that the inverse-limit resolution stabilizes degreewise. This is an explicit higher resolution construction, rather than an application of abstract resolution existence.

title: The first Tor defect of the cotangent complex of a tensor product
difficulty_reason: The proof computes the derived failure of cotangent base change using degree-two Lichtenbaum-Schlessinger relations. It compares relation modules after tensoring, quotients out trivial relations, and identifies the cokernel as Tor rather than merely obtaining a vanishing bound. The required compatibility between the explicit complexes and derived tensoring is central.

title: The transitivity triangle for cotangent complexes of sheaves of rings
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs compatible standard resolutions and an exact simplicial differential sequence when the second map is injective. It identifies the final term through two quasi-isomorphisms, then uses sheafification and a product-ring replacement to handle arbitrary homomorphisms. This is the global construction of the canonical triangle, with nontrivial resolution compatibility.

title: Essential Artinian surjections characterized by cotangent differentials
difficulty_reason: The converse constructs the kernel of a projected derivation as a subalgebra and proves it still surjects onto the target. Essential surjectivity then forces the projected differential kernel to vanish. The final small-extension argument turns nonessentiality into an actual section through a length comparison.

title: Smooth morphisms of prorepresentable functors are power-series extensions
difficulty_reason: The proof lifts a relative cotangent-space isomorphism successively through Artinian quotients to obtain a map into a power-series ring. It then constructs a section and uses complete-local cotangent-space surjectivity twice to prove both maps are inverse isomorphisms. The formal smoothness characterization requires this completed lifting and rigidity construction.

title: Existence of a smooth complete local base with prescribed cotangent sequence
difficulty_reason: For a possibly inseparable residue extension, the proof successively slices a smooth algebra to eliminate nonzero differential classes. Completing the resulting local algebra preserves its cotangent data and formal smoothness. This constructs a base whose cotangent sequence has the asserted two isomorphisms, beyond the simpler separable finite-etale construction.

title: Existence of versal formal objects under Schlessinger conditions
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a descending sequence of minimal lifting ideals inside a power-series ring and takes its complete quotient. It then proves versality by analyzing an arbitrary small-extension pullback, distinguishing split and essential surjections, and forcing its kernel to contain the next minimal ideal. The inductive construction and the universal lifting argument are both substantive.

title: Power-series splitting of a versal object over its minimal descent ring
difficulty_reason: The proof first obtains a retraction onto the minimal descent subring and proves its restriction is an automorphism. Versality then produces sections at every Artinian order, forcing the resulting power-series map to be an isomorphism. A separate smooth-descent argument proves the descended object remains versal.

title: Minimal versal tangent maps are bijective modulo residue-field derivations
difficulty_reason: The proof detects a nontrivial tangent kernel outside the residue-derivation orbits and forms the kernel subring of that derivation. It decomposes the first-order algebra as a dual-number product and uses the Schlessinger lifting condition to descend the object to a proper subring. This contradicts minimality and establishes the orbit-level injectivity even for inseparable residue fields.

title: Rim gluing for quotients of smooth groupoids in functors
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs an explicit quotient fibre square by lifting an arrow through the smooth source map. It then checks both commutativity and the universal property, reconstructing the unique mediating arrow from the Rim gluing property of the arrow functor. This is effective two-categorical gluing for a quotient, rather than formal preservation of a property.

title: Versal formal objects after a finite extension of the residue field
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a formally smooth completed polynomial extension realizing the new residue field. It then defines a natural transformation into the residue-change functor and verifies its lifting property against arbitrary Artinian surjections using continuous formal smoothness. This establishes compatibility of versality with the nontrivial change-of-residue-field construction.

title: Relative perfectness and finite complexes of flat modules
difficulty_reason: The reverse finiteness implication descends the algebra and flat module to a Noetherian finite-type model, resolves there, and checks that base change preserves exactness. The other direction truncates a finite-free representative at a Tor-amplitude bound, identifying a flat final cokernel.

title: Power annihilation of Ext and local projectivity of a two-term derived object
difficulty_reason: The author uses a cohomological triangle and injective targets to separate the negative cohomology obstruction from near-projectivity of degree-zero cohomology. A localized universal extension class and uniform radical-power estimates recover the converse from projectivity off the ideal locus.

title: Pro-isomorphisms preserve inverse limits and their first derived functors
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs chain maps between product presentations using summed transition operators, rather than merely passing to limits. It then gives explicit coboundaries proving independence of a representative and invariance of the first derived limit under cofinal reindexing.

title: Emmanouil criterion for Mittag-Leffler inverse systems
difficulty_reason: Failure of Mittag-Leffler is encoded by a sequence of elements escaping stabilized images. The proof builds either an element of a product/direct-sum quotient that cannot lift to an inverse limit or an explicit nonzero derived-limit class, establishing the converse by a substantive obstruction construction.

title: Strictification of inverse systems of derived objects
difficulty_reason: The author replaces each derived transition map by a roof and constructs quasi-isomorphic chain-level representatives inductively. The new transition maps must be actual maps of complexes compatible with the existing system, producing a single derived object in the category of module systems.

title: Exact recovery complex for modules under flat neighbourhood gluing
difficulty_reason: The author proves injectivity using ideal-power torsion and the unchanged infinitesimal neighbourhood. Its computational converse tracks a compatible tuple through a Koszul-homology obstruction, uses flatness to identify that obstruction with its base change, and recovers the tuple from one module element.

title: Beauville-Laszlo gluing equivalence for modules
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs the glued module as the kernel of a surjective difference map. It separates power torsion from the torsion-free quotient, controls Tor under base change and uses a comparison diagram to recover both local pieces, proving full faithfulness and essential surjectivity.

title: Construction of derived completion as a reflective subcategory
difficulty_reason: The author constructs completion by derived Hom from an extended Cech complex. Localization annihilates that complex in the relevant directions, proving derived completeness, and a triangle argument verifies the full universal mapping property rather than just defining a candidate object.

title: Derived complete power-torsion modules have bounded torsion
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces to a nonzerodivisor principal ideal and represents the module by a quotient of complete torsion-free modules. A Baire-category argument and an open-mapping theorem promote pointwise power torsion to one uniform annihilating power.

title: Controlled Ext factorizations for powers of an ideal
difficulty_reason: The author chooses compatible presentations for a module and its ideal-power submodules and controls the syzygy comparison by Artin-Rees. A diagram proves the first-Ext factorization, and dimension shifting inductively supplies a uniform loss of ideal powers in every higher degree.

title: Weak dimension one and local valuation-ring structure
difficulty_reason: The proof passes from flat ideals to arbitrary submodules of flat modules using filtered free approximations and a filtration by ideals. It then uses local finite-flat freeness to prove the local ring is a domain with principal finitely generated ideals, establishing the valuation-ring characterization in both directions.

title: Olivier rigidity theorem for weakly etale local maps
difficulty_reason: The proof shows every fibre has exactly one point with unchanged residue field. A hypothetical splitting yields an idempotent after an algebraic field extension, while integral closure over the strictly henselian base forces a local subring that excludes that idempotent; the map is then shown to be a faithfully flat epimorphism.

title: Smooth local maps preserve numbers of geometric branches
difficulty_reason: The author compares minimal primes after henselization and strict henselization using flat going down. Normalization and integral tensor products prove uniqueness of a prime above each base branch, with a separate residue-field argument required for the non-geometric assertion.

title: Disconnected punctured spectra of completions and henselizations
difficulty_reason: The proof encodes a disconnected completed punctured spectrum by two ideals with nilpotent product and finite-length conormal data. It algebraizes a quotient, uses henselian etale localization to descend its ideal, and reconstructs the disconnected decomposition before completion.

title: Failure of formal catenarity obstructs universal catenarity
difficulty_reason: The proof chooses a smallest-dimensional completed component and algebraizes its quotient to contradict the dimension formula. For larger component dimension it chooses a perturbing parameter by prime avoidance and descends the defect inductively.

title: Galois action on primes and residue automorphisms in infinite extensions
difficulty_reason: The proof uses a maximal compatible pair of a Galois subfield and an automorphism moving a prescribed prime. Finite normal extensions and correction by a stabilizer force enlargement; a second construction simultaneously matches the prescribed residue-field automorphism.

title: Wild inertia and the tame inertia character
difficulty_reason: The author constructs a uniformizer-independent character of inertia into roots of unity and identifies its kernel through the associated graded ring. A filtration calculation forces kernel elements to have p-power order, and a formally etale residue-field splitting proves the second-order description under separability.

title: Abhyankar lemma for tame extensions of discrete valuation rings
difficulty_reason: The proof first kills a unit factor through a finite etale extension and descends the desired formal smoothness. It then reduces to adjoining a root of a uniformizer, computes ramification indices and residue separability after normalization, and proves that the new local extensions are unramified.

title: Tame ramification is preserved under normal closure and compositum
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces tame extensions to unramified extensions after adjoining a root of a uniformizer. For normal closure it explicitly analyzes normalized tensor powers, constructs the root-of-unity ratio algebra, and proves that all resulting field factors remain tame.

title: Elimination of ramification for essentially finite-type valuation-ring extensions
difficulty_reason: The author perfects the residue field through a filtered union of weakly unramified extensions and combines Epp solutions for all resulting branches. It then descends the solution to a finite field-extension stage by stabilizing spectra, uniformizers and separable residue-field generators.

title: Unique factorization in regular local rings
difficulty_reason: The proof inducts on dimension and makes a height-one prime invertible after inverting a regular parameter. Vanishing of the relevant Picard group supplies a generator there, which is descended using irreducible factorization and the behavior of prime elements under localization.

title: Descent of roots up to units through codimension-one unramified maps
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a fractional-valuation ideal from the required divided orders at height-one primes. Tensoring and normal-domain intersection criteria show that ideal becomes principal upstairs, and faithfully flat descent supplies the desired root downstairs.

title: Etale local extensions of valuation rings are weakly unramified
difficulty_reason: After proving valuation-ring structure from weak dimension, the proof must show equality of value groups. It approximates the base by normal Noetherian local subrings and descends roots up to units through codimension-one unramified extensions, recovering the value-group statement.

title: Finitely presented modules over generalized valuation rings
difficulty_reason: The proof finds a generator whose annihilator remains minimal for every lift of its residue class. It proves the cyclic submodule is relatively divisible by comparing totally ordered principal ideals, splits off that summand and inducts to obtain a cyclic decomposition.

title: Reduced hypersurfaces through prescribed divisors of a normal surface
difficulty_reason: The author bounds the number of divisorial components under small perturbations and chooses a perturbation maximizing that number. Carefully selected symbolic-power valuations then force every component multiplicity to one without introducing new components, producing a reduced hypersurface through all prescribed divisors.

title: Prescribed sections with controlled codimension of degeneracy
difficulty_reason: A double induction constructs auxiliary sections avoiding generic points of the existing bad components. Chinese-remainder interpolation combines them while preserving prescribed fibre values, and a component-by-component argument raises the codimension of every new degeneracy locus.

title: Bass freeness theorem for countably generated infinite-rank projectives
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs an increasing sequence of finite stably free direct summands capturing all generators. It then extracts an infinite free summand by successive good-element choices and applies an Eilenberg swindle to absorb the complementary countably generated projective module.

title: Etale acyclicity of absolutely integrally closed rings for finite constant coefficients
difficulty_reason: Higher acyclicity must be reduced to a degree-one obstruction on a two-open cover without assuming the ring is a domain. The proof constructs an interpolating section in an auxiliary group scheme on the intersecting closures, then glues over scheme-theoretic unions to trivialize the torsor.

title: Smooth base change for prime-to-characteristic torsion etale cohomology
difficulty_reason: The proof must efface pulled-back injective sheaf cohomology, despite pullback not preserving injectivity.
