It reduces to relative curves, approximates by finite-type bases, passes through finite normalizations and controlled Galois covers of the generic fibre, then combines degree induction and dimension induction to kill the remaining support.

title: Two-dimensional tame-symbol reciprocity for nonzerodivisors in Noetherian local rings
difficulty_reason: The proof must establish cancellation over all height-one primes without assuming the local ring is regular or normal. Finite local extensions normalize the chosen factorizations, and a periodic complex with finite-length discrepancy is used to identify each tame-symbol order with a periodic Euler invariant whose sum vanishes.

title: Chow homology descent exact sequence for proper completely decomposed envelopes
difficulty_reason: Surjectivity requires locally finite birational lifts of all cycle supports, including supports of rational-equivalence relations. The kernel must then be represented by cycles on the double fibre product, with explicit generic components and degree cancellation distinguishing equal-dimensional and lower-dimensional images.

title: Dimension-filtered coherent Grothendieck groups identify with cycle groups
difficulty_reason: The proof must recover the coherent class from all generic-point lengths, including infinitely many locally finite supports. It globalizes generic composition series, constructs coherent direct sums of successive filtration layers, and compares these with structure sheaves by extended ideal subsheaves whose cokernels have lower-dimensional support.

title: Rational-equivalence cycle classes vanish in the adjacent coherent Grothendieck quotient
difficulty_reason: A principal divisor must be represented by a difference of coherent quotient sheaves even when its rational function is not globally regular. The proof constructs the ideal of denominators and compares two injections of that ideal, then verifies every codimension-one coefficient through the order/length distance identity.

title: Gysin pullbacks for line-bundle sections commute on Chow homology
difficulty_reason: The proof must compare intersection cycles when their supports meet the divisor centres improperly. Carefully normalized meromorphic sections reduce the difference to tame-symbol divisors, and one must show every resulting rational-equivalence support lies inside the common centre rather than merely vanishes after pushforward to the ambient scheme.

title: Chow pullback is surjective for Zariski-locally trivial affine-space bundles
difficulty_reason: The proof must reduce an arbitrary cycle to pullbacks while controlling locally finite image supports. Dimension induction and localization first reduce to a product affine line, where a generic irreducible polynomial makes every nonglobal component rationally trivial after shrinking and moves the remaining cycle to a lower-dimensional boundary.

title: Projective bundle formula for Chow homology of finite locally free modules
difficulty_reason: Injectivity requires successively extracting every coefficient by Chern-class cap and proper pushforward. Surjectivity must be built by reduction to irreducible support and induction on the base dimension, followed by an affine-stratum filtration of the trivialized projective bundle and explicit lifts of cycle coefficients.

title: Top Chern class equals the zero-cycle class for sections with expected dimension and generic regularity
difficulty_reason: The proof must preserve the zero-locus multiplicities while reducing the vector-bundle rank. Pullback to the projective bundle produces a line-bundle quotient section and a lower-rank section on its zero locus; regular-sequence control and fibre-dimension estimates are needed to justify the induction.

title: Chern invariants of locally bounded vector-bundle complexes depend only on their derived object
difficulty_reason: Two representatives need not be termwise comparable globally, so the proof modifies each integral test scheme until the cohomology has Tor dimension at most one. It then compares the resulting vector-bundle resolutions through a Schanuel-type fibre-product construction, using bivariant detection to recover global independence.

title: Localized Chern classes satisfy triangle additivity under rank and representability hypotheses
difficulty_reason: The proof must establish multiplicativity in the supported bivariant group, including all listed representability alternatives. It deforms a triangle map by a scalar over the affine line to compare the cone with the direct sum, then combines two graph constructions over a common fibre product to prove the product formula there.

title: Gysin classes compose for compatible exact sequences of virtual normal sheaves
difficulty_reason: The proof must compare the normal-cone definitions for nested centres with excess normal directions. A simultaneous blowup reduces both centres to Cartier divisors, top-Chern factors remove the excess bundle, and a cartesian cone diagram identifies the two fundamental cone cycles under the remaining zero-section pullback.

title: Rational coherent K theory agrees with Chow homology for schemes embedded in regular quasi-compact schemes
difficulty_reason: The localized Chern character must be proved triangular for the support-dimension filtration, not simply assumed to be an isomorphism. The proof tracks supports of arbitrary coherent classes and determines the leading coefficient of every integral support by reduction to a generic regular-sequence embedding, yielding inverse maps on all graded pieces.

title: Smooth targets identify bivariant Chow groups with degree-shifted bivariant groups
difficulty_reason: The inverse to composition with a smooth Gysin class must be constructed rather than inferred from flat pullback. The proof uses the relative diagonal and two cartesian restriction diagrams, then verifies both compositions by diagonal-section identities and bivariant Gysin compatibility.

title: Periodic Euler lengths equal orders of generic periodic determinants on one-dimensional support
difficulty_reason: The proof must reconcile finite-length cohomology with determinant scalars at all minimal support primes. After separating generic supports, carefully chosen good sequences in kernels and images must be lifted and adjusted to satisfy annihilator conditions, then compared through a common lattice so all length discrepancies exactly match the determinant order.

title: Tensoring a coherent sheaf by a line bundle realizes first-Chern cap in the filtered K quotient
difficulty_reason: Embedded associated points prevent the naive meromorphic-section quotient argument. The proof removes those points through two support-dimension stages, replaces the sheaf by one on its annihilator subscheme, and builds two denominator-ideal quotient sheaves whose cycle difference gives the first-Chern action while remaining in the prescribed K-theory subgroup.

title: Cycle-level projection formula for flat proper maps of nonsingular varieties
difficulty_reason: The proof must establish proper intersection on the target and match multiplicities before passing to Chow groups. It separates positive-dimensional generic fibres from generically finite supports, uses properness to obtain local finiteness near each intersection component, and compares Tor lengths through the derived projection formula at those stalks.

title: General projective projections are locally immersions or etale at a fixed nonsingular point
difficulty_reason: One must produce one nonempty parameter open avoiding both secant identifications and tangent collapse. The proof constructs two incidence schemes with strict dimension bounds, removes their constructible images, and then combines finiteness, tangent injectivity and the single-fibre criterion to obtain a local immersion or etaleness.

title: Intersection of properly meeting cycles on nonsingular projective varieties respects rational equivalence
difficulty_reason: The cycles in a rational-equivalence presentation need not meet the fixed cycle properly even when the total cycle does. The proof inducts on excess intersection dimension, uses a moving construction to lower every bad intersection simultaneously, and compares the fibres of a projective one-parameter family while preserving properness at both endpoints.

title: Uniform projective reconstruction for flat proper finite-presentation thickenings with an ample lift
difficulty_reason: One twist bound must work for every thickening in the statement, not just for a chosen deformation. The proof uses perfect cohomology and base change to transfer vanishing and local freeness, then proves finite presentation of the reconstructed graded algebra by Noetherian approximation while correcting the mismatch between two independent degree bounds.

title: Smooth morphisms are exactly locally finitely presented formally smooth morphisms
difficulty_reason: Affine formal lifting does not automatically glue to a scheme morphism on the whole affine test thickening. The proof constructs the sheaf of lifts as a torsor under the internal Hom of differentials and conormal modules, proves local solvability, and uses quasi-coherent H1 vanishing to obtain a global lift.

title: Pushouts of scheme thickenings along affine morphisms exist as schemes
difficulty_reason: The fibre product of structure sheaves must first be proved to define a scheme, not merely a ringed-space pushout. The proof identifies its local affine rings and localized sections through a nilpotent fibre-product calculation, then glues the local universal mapping properties to establish the global pushout.

title: Closed immersions between smooth schemes are etale-locally standard coordinate embeddings
difficulty_reason: The construction must simultaneously lift etale coordinates on the closed subscheme and keep the defining regular sequence as transverse coordinates. The resulting map is shown etale by a fibrewise miracle-flatness argument that matches local dimensions and controls the finite residual fibre.

title: Relative associated points specialize with constant component dimension under flatness
difficulty_reason: The proof must transfer relative associatedness and fibre dimension along a specialization without Noetherian base hypotheses. A valuation-ring base change reduces the problem to an injectivity contradiction: prime avoidance supplies a special-fibre nonzerodivisor whose flatness lift contradicts generic associatedness.

title: Fibrewise nonzerodivisors extend to flat relative Cartier slices for flat finitely presented morphisms
difficulty_reason: The local equation must remain a nonzerodivisor on an actual neighbourhood and the hypersurface quotient must remain flat. The proof descends the equation and morphism to a Noetherian model, checks the fibre condition through a faithfully flat local map, and brings a uniformly localized exact flat sequence back to the original base.

title: Scheme-theoretic density in a generic fibre spreads over an open subset of an irreducible base
difficulty_reason: A topologically dense open need not detect embedded or nilpotent structure, so a finite algebraic injectivity test must be built. The proof encodes the generic density by multiplication with finitely many functions, applies generic flatness to the algebra and cokernel, and transports the exact injection to every fibre on the chosen open.

title: Relative associated points persist generically along their closures for finite-type morphisms
difficulty_reason: One must turn a fibrewise associated prime into a globally embedded cyclic module after generic flatness. A second generic-flatness step makes the cokernel flat so that the injection survives every fibre, allowing all generic points of the resulting fibre supports to be recognized as associated points.

title: Geometric connectedness of the generic fibre spreads for finite-type morphisms over irreducible bases
difficulty_reason: The proof first passes to an étale base change making generic components geometrically irreducible. It then spreads their closures and their pairwise incidence graph simultaneously, using flatness of the nonempty intersections to preserve the graph and connectedness over every geometric fibre.

title: The fibre component containing a section is locally a neighbourhood at a geometrically reduced fibre in flat finitely presented families
difficulty_reason: Noetherian approximation must preserve the section, flatness and geometric reducedness before a constructible-neighbourhood criterion can be used. The proof realizes every generalization by a discrete valuation ring and controls connected components there, showing that the selected fibre component is stable under the necessary generalizations.

title: Weak relative Noether normalization by a quasi-finite polynomial-algebra map with the maximal fibre dimension
difficulty_reason: Approximation must preserve the global fibre-dimension bound while reducing to finite-type integer algebras. A double induction then constructs a coordinate dropping all fibre dimensions, first by transcendence at generic components and then by the perturbation a^n+b to reconcile an open stratum with its closed complement.

title: A generic linear combination preserves geometric irreducibility under the stated algebraic-independence hypotheses
difficulty_reason: The proof must exclude all new separable algebraic elements over the generic linear-combination field. Translation automorphisms and finiteness of intermediate separable fields force the required invariance, while an additional transcendental parameter handles finite ground fields.

title: Generic triviality of a line bundle extends over proper flat finitely presented valuation-ring families with integral closed fibre and one-dimensional generic global sections
difficulty_reason: The proof identifies global sections over a valuation ring as a free rank-one lattice inside the generic sections. It then rules out vanishing of its generator on the closed fibre by a divisibility argument and uses the relative effective-Cartier criterion to show that its zero locus is empty.

title: Simultaneous étale approximation of relative completed local maps over a locally Noetherian G-ring base
difficulty_reason: Both the base map and the relative map must be approximated while preserving their compatibility to a prescribed adic order. The proof combines local-map approximation with Popescu smoothing and finite-presentation descent to transport an étale model through a smooth intermediate algebra before specializing it back to an elementary étale neighbourhood.

title: Étale-local product splitting of integral algebras with finite fibres and finite separable residue extensions
difficulty_reason: The proof first captures every separable residue-field generator in a finite subalgebra while preserving distinct fibre primes. Étale splitting of that finite subalgebra must then be transferred to the original integral algebra, removing the unwanted summand without losing the purely inseparable residue-field condition.

title: The quasi-finite locus of a separated finite-type morphism is an open subscheme of its relative normalization
difficulty_reason: The proof must identify the whole inverse image of an open normalization neighbourhood, not merely embed the quasi-finite locus. Elementary étale splitting isolates a finite component, normalization respects the resulting disjoint union, and descent of the local isomorphism completes the global identification.

title: Every quasi-finite morphism becomes finite over a dense open of its target
difficulty_reason: The morphism need not be separated, so generic finiteness of affine charts is insufficient. The proof removes images of overlap boundaries to make the chart intersections closed and recover separatedness, then descends properness from a finite chart cover to establish finiteness.

title: Universal degree stratification for separated flat locally finitely presented quasi-finite morphisms with universally bounded fibres
difficulty_reason: The maximal-degree locus must be shown open with finite locally free restriction by étale splitting and elimination of the residual component. Induction on the degree must also prove the universal property for arbitrary nonreduced test schemes, using reduction and universal closedness to recover finiteness.

title: Étale covers of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes admit finite finitely presented surjective refinements that factor locally through the cover
difficulty_reason: Induction on geometric fibre cardinalities must construct an integral cover despite the boundary of an étale open immersion. The proof separates the diagonal component, extends a smaller-degree refinement across the boundary, and finally descends its local factorization data to a finite finitely presented approximation.

title: Vertical locally principal subschemes occupy fibre components under the irreducible dominant finite-type and nonincreasing fibre-dimension hypotheses
difficulty_reason: The Noetherian argument combines the principal ideal theorem with specialization chains and the fibre-dimension bound. The general case requires a careful finite-type integer-algebra approximation preserving generic invertibility, both fibre dimensions and avoidance of all minimal primes, so that the same contradiction descends.

title: Closed fibre points interpolating a specialization are dense for locally finite-type morphisms
difficulty_reason: A valuation-ring reduction must preserve the original generic fibre and the closedness of the special point. Dimension induction then chooses a principal slice avoiding arbitrary closed subsets and all special-fibre components, using the vertical-divisor criterion to ensure a horizontal component through the special point.

title: Proper open-and-closed fibre pieces lift as proper open-and-closed pieces over henselian pairs in separated finite-type families
difficulty_reason: Chow modification and projective closure must transport the desired component without introducing an overlapping boundary. Henselianity rules out the closed intersections and boundary pieces, after which Stein factorization and lifting of integral-algebra idempotents construct the proper component.

title: Cokernels of finite modules over two finite-type algebras become flat over a localized Noetherian domain
difficulty_reason: The cokernel need not be finite over either algebra in the usable form, so ordinary generic flatness alone is insufficient. A prime filtration reduces to a domain, generic freeness embeds the finite source in a finite free summand after localization, and control of the entire localization quotient establishes universal injectivity.

title: Finite-presentation scheme-theoretic images commute with arbitrary base change on a finite closed stratification after a finite-type thickening of the base
difficulty_reason: Noetherian approximation and induction must produce a finite stratification with finite-type defining ideals over the original quasi-compact quasi-separated base. On every generic stratum, cokernel flatness and simultaneous flatness of the two algebras ensure kernel formation commutes with all tensor products, then affine-local image descriptions globalize this condition.

title: Finitely presented families over reduced bases admit smooth strata near a generic point after a finite locally free radicial cover
difficulty_reason: A purely inseparable extension of the generic residue field must be realized by a tower of finite locally free universally injective covers on an open neighbourhood. The proof then descends all generic closed strata simultaneously and shrinks to preserve closed immersion, thickening and smoothness conditions.

title: Separated finitely presented families of generic dimension at most one admit radicially altered smooth proper curve models with finite normalization maps
difficulty_reason: The proof spreads a generic normalization and smooth projective completion after realizing its inseparable field extension on the base. It must simultaneously preserve finite surjectivity, étale component bases, smooth proper geometrically connected completions, and a fibrewise dense open on which the normalization map is a thickening.

title: Separated locally quasi-finite scheme morphisms satisfy effective fppf descent
difficulty_reason: A locally quasi-finite object need not itself be quasi-compact, so quasi-affine descent cannot be applied globally. The proof saturates each affine open under the descent isomorphism, proves the saturation quasi-compact and invariant using the cocycle, descends these quasi-affine pieces and glues their effective descent data.

title: Pseudo-coherent morphisms are syntomic local on the source
difficulty_reason: The proof must descend pseudo-coherence through a syntomic cover rather than only through a fixed flat base change. It lifts the cover across a polynomial embedding, chooses a principal neighbourhood where the lift is faithfully flat, and translates pseudo-coherence to the defining ideal for faithfully flat module descent.

title: Scheme pushouts along closed immersions and integral morphisms exist under the stated affine-neighbourhood compatibility hypothesis
difficulty_reason: The topological pushout with its fibre-product structure sheaf must be proved locally affine at every glued point. Compatible affine neighbourhoods reduce this to a ring fibre product whose localizations, integral projection and tensor-product identity are checked, and the local pushout universal properties must then descend globally.

title: Derived Chow lemma for separated finitely presented schemes over arbitrary rings
difficulty_reason: A graph closure over a Noetherian approximation constructs the geometric modification and a coherent supported object. Pulling this object back to the original base requires an explicit Tor-independence argument to retain its structure-sheaf identification on the prescribed projective open, while preserving pseudo-coherence and support.

title: Proper one-dimensional morphisms with fibrewise vanishing first cohomology and surjective structure-sheaf pushforward retain these properties universally near the fibre
difficulty_reason: The proof must establish finite generation of the pushforward over a possibly non-Noetherian and infinitely generated target before applying Nakayama. An ambient polynomial embedding, Tor-independent derived base change and Noetherian approximation supply pseudo-coherence and finiteness, allowing fibrewise surjectivity to spread with universal cohomology vanishing.

title: Locally quasi-finite componentwise dominant morphisms to geometrically unibranch locally Noetherian schemes are universally open
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces universal openness to lifting generalizations and isolates a finite component after elementary étale base change. Geometric unibranchness forces the component image to fill the local target, so closedness of the finite map and uniqueness of its special point produce the required lift.

title: Pushout descent of objects of an algebraic stack
difficulty_reason: The proof glues smooth algebraic-space presentations across a thickening and transfers their compatible maps into a representing space by the pushout universal property. Essential surjectivity is constructed on a new smooth cover and combined with the fully faithful descent calculation.

title: A single-point square-zero obstruction to versality
difficulty_reason: A failure of formal versality is converted into an actual square-zero thickening of an affine neighbourhood by pushing out a small Artinian extension. The proof then shows that any local retraction would factor through a finite infinitesimal neighbourhood and contradict the selected lifting obstruction.

title: Construction of a universal dual obstruction class
difficulty_reason: The proof builds a split extension from the universal polynomial presentation and lifts its obstruction through the naive cotangent complex. It then adjusts the resulting cohomology class by a controlled ambiguity so that its tangent specialization equals the canonical deformation, using a short exact sequence of deformation situations.

title: Lefschetz cohomology comparison through the punctured affine cone
difficulty_reason: The argument transfers the depth inequality to the cone through the two possible fibre-point types of a one-dimensional smooth torsor. Local cohomology annihilation and completion yield a comparison on the cone, and compatible graded decompositions recover the required proper-scheme cohomology comparison.

title: Generic separable degrees define weightings for locally quasi-finite morphisms over geometrically unibranch locally Noetherian bases

The proof decomposes a finite algebra over the strict henselization, uses the unique minimal prime supplied by geometric unibranchness, and matches the resulting weighted sum with the geometric generic-fibre cardinality.

title: Weightings on quasi-finite finitely presented affine morphisms descend through inverse limits
difficulty_reason: Descending the constructible level sets does not by itself descend the weighting condition. The proof uses a universal finite open-and-closed test neighbourhood to encode that condition as local constancy, then descends openness of its finitely many level sets at a later stage.

title: The maximal weighted-fibre locus of a quasi-finite finitely presented affine morphism with positive weighting is affine
difficulty_reason: The proof combines Noetherian approximation of the weighting with finite surjective affineness descent. After replacing the finite compactification by a union of sections, it computes how generic weights specialize and identifies the maximal locus as an intersection of affine section images.

title: Quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes admit proper finitely presented completely decomposed covers with ample families of line bundles
difficulty_reason: The proof must preserve residue-field lifts while arranging an ample family on the covering scheme. Noetherian approximation reduces to finite-dimensional schemes, where an admissible blowup handles a dense open and dimension induction supplies a complementary proper cover with the same residue-field lifting property.

title: Riemann–Hurwitz multiplicities and the tame equality criterion for generically étale smooth proper curves with ground-field global functions
difficulty_reason: The proof must treat inseparable residue fields uniformly rather than only differentiate a separable local uniformizer. Base change of the Gorenstein different reduces the calculation to an Artinian fibre algebra, where the trace element detects tame ramification and its annihilator determines the exact different ideal.

title: Smooth proper curves of genus at least two have separable closed points of degree at most twice the genus minus two
difficulty_reason: The usual canonical pencil yields a degree bound but may be inseparable over an imperfect ground field. The proof rules out its Frobenius-factorization alternative using linear-series bounds on the Frobenius twist, then chooses a rational point in the étale locus of the resulting pencil.

title: Finite algebraic modifications over algebraically closed fields supported at finitely many points factor into point gluings and tangent-vector contractions
difficulty_reason: Induction must construct intermediate scheme algebras while strictly decreasing the finite-length discrepancy. Reduction to a single support point and analysis of the intermediate residue algebra isolate the two minimal algebra extensions, corresponding to gluing points or collapsing a tangent vector.

title: Nodes on algebraic curves over arbitrary fields are characterized by quadratic completion, Fitting ideals and geometric branches with delta invariant one
difficulty_reason: The equivalence must descend residue-field separability and the Fitting-ideal condition from geometric fibres. The proof then reconciles completion normal forms with normalization lengths and geometric branch counts, including the strict control of delta invariants under field extension.

title: A flat finite-type family over a Noetherian local base has completed equation xy=h at a split node of its fibre
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs compatible lifts of the two branch parameters by successive corrections in every power of the base maximal ideal. title: Fixed-mass H1 convergence of positive radial three-dimensional Choquard ground states and their frequencies for smooth autocorrelation potentials approaching the Newton kernel
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.222
difficulty_reason: Radial compactness by itself gives weak H1 and strong intermediate-Lp limits but can lose the prescribed L2 mass. The source controls the nonscale-invariant potentials through their local L3/2 and far-field uniform parts, passes the nonlinear equation to the limit and uses the positive limiting frequency to recover the entire mass. Only after that recovery and the energy identity does it promote the gradient convergence to strong H1 convergence, a remaining nonlocal perturbation obligation beyond the allowed radial compactness and Newton uniqueness foundations.

title: Classification of intermediate boundary crossed-product algebras for finite-center lattices with injective dense projections in product groups satisfying quasi-center and boundary-freeness hypotheses
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.223
difficulty_reason: The prior noncommutative boundary dichotomy does not identify the factor-continuous elements inside this particular crossed product. Section2 constructs boundary-contraction sequences avoiding the required centralizers and uses Fourier-coefficient estimates to prove that identification. The finite-center corner then transfers it to the correct quotient algebra before factor reconstruction applies, so the new retained core is more than the final invocation of the existing factor theorem.

title: Coexistence of positive metric entropy and elliptic islands for analytic symplectomorphisms of closed analytic symplectic surfaces
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.224
difficulty_reason: Analytic bump functions are unavailable, so the desired coexistence cannot be produced by ordinary local smooth pasting. The source constructs an analytic symplectic blow-up, compatible involution quotient and Hamiltonian cap, then blows down the cap boundary while preserving the stochastic piece. It proves the collar gluing and performs the sphere/torus/pants constructions for all genera, remaining substantive surgery obligations after the stated normal-form foundations are allowed.

title: Complex rational maps of degree at least two whose periodic multipliers all lie in one number field are power, Chebyshev or Lattes maps
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.227
difficulty_reason: Equidistribution of Galois orbits applies only after the multiplier-isospectral moduli point has been descended to a number field. The source constructs periodic cycles shadowing a chosen repeller while tracking their periods and characteristic exponents, rather than merely quoting the needed periodic approximation. It then combines those cycles with the arithmetic orbit bounds and exponent rigidity to obtain the exceptional classification, leaving a new dynamical construction beyond the cited equidistribution and rigidity foundations.

title: L2 stability of square roots of bounded positive three-dimensional Coulomb or gravitational Vlasov-Poisson solutions with mixed derivative control
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.230
difficulty_reason: Passing to square roots does not by itself close an L2 stability estimate for the Coulomb field. The author decomposes the singular interaction into two terms and bounds one by endpoint Lorentz control, while the other requires Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev, velocity Cauchy-Schwarz and a different spatial mixed-norm estimate. Those two source-specific closures produce the exact integrated coefficient before the routine Gronwall step, rather than treating Gronwall or the advanced equation name as the difficulty.

title: A complex analytic monic cubic 3-web germ with distinct generic directions, unequal-weight linear symmetry, identically zero normalized Chern connection and the specified commuting lifted idempotents reconstructs a Frobenius 3-fold germ with isotropic unity
source_version: Official SIGMA 8 (2012) article 078, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2012.078; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof reconstructs an invariant metric and multiplication from multivalued web-root fields, then turns their commutativity and normalized connection equations into a compatible system for an analytic associativity potential. The weight matching and potential reconstruction produce holomorphic Frobenius tensors through the singular web point, a nonlinear geometric inverse construction beyond ordinary qualification differential geometry.

title: A nondegenerate continuous C0(T)-algebra over a locally compact Hausdorff base, with a fibre-preserving strongly continuous symplectic-vector-group action, remains a covariant continuous field under fixed Rieffel deformation, with each fibre canonically deformed
source_version: Official SIGMA 8 (2012) article 091, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2012.091; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof must preserve the nondegenerate central base action through a multiplier-algebra deformation, which requires Dixmier-Malliavin factorization and explicit smooth-ideal regularization estimates. It then identifies the deformed fibre ideals and proves lower semicontinuity through invariant primitive-ideal hulls and openness, substantive noncommutative topology and analysis beyond ordinary qualification C-star theory.

title: Explicit unitary decomposition of the quasi-regular representation of a connected simply connected nonabelian one-parameter metabelian nilpotent Lie group modulo a discrete cocompact subgroup
source_version: Official SIGMA 7 (2011) article 021, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2011.021; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The author constructs a global representation intertwiner by Fourier coefficients along a rational codimension-one abelian subgroup, and organizes its infinite-dimensional induced summands through lattice coadjoint orbits. The proof establishes the rational subgroup needed for an arbitrary lattice, proves the Parseval isometry, and constructs an explicit periodized inverse on a dense subspace. This combines nilpotent orbit theory with lattice and Hilbert-space reconstruction beyond ordinary qualifying-exam Fourier or representation arguments.

title: Uniform perimeter improvement of planar radial cluster stars with more than three rays for strictly convex anisotropic densities smooth in direction
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.238
difficulty_reason: Euclidean120-degree junction arguments do not establish a competitor for a nonsymmetric anisotropic perimeter, whose exterior and interior interfaces have different costs. The source constructs competitors in all white/colored configurations and uses first-order tangent estimates to rule out the nondegenerate cases, then builds a separate three-segment competitor for the degenerate four-sector case. The small-angle reduction and compactness turn these strict improvements into a uniform positive gain, leaving a complete geometric construction beyond routine convexity terminology.

title: Polynomial-index weakly symplectic or unitary lattice bases for integral-trace skew-Hermitian forms over Albert type I or II division algebras
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.240
difficulty_reason: The quoted class-index version of Minkowski does not provide a basis compatible with the skew-Hermitian form while keeping polynomial discriminant bounds. The authors extract small nondegenerate rank-one or rank-two modules, control the complementary lattice and repeat the construction through distinct field and quaternion cases with explicit index and pairing-size estimates. They also bound the failure of involution-stability of the stabilizer order to remove the extra induction parameter, a nonroutine quantitative arithmetic construction before the later formal applications.

title: Highest-weight critical-exponent lower bound for the symmetric limit-set Hausdorff dimension of strongly projectively convex-cocompact subgroups of SL(n,R)
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.241
difficulty_reason: Coornaert’s visual-boundary dimension theorem alone does not compare the Euclidean dimension of the symmetric projective limit set with the highest-weight critical exponent. The authors prove a uniform primal-dual boundary estimate from Hilbert cross ratios, supporting hyperplanes and angle bounds, controlling both point and tangent-hyperplane distances. This new geometric comparison supplies the required dimension inequality before the formal entropy and Hausdorff-dimension conclusion.

title: Polynomial lower bounds for nonzero algebraic-integer linear combinations of E-function values over a fixed number field at algebraic points
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.249
difficulty_reason: Shidlovskii's quoted quantitative theorem applies to rational-coefficient E-functions and cannot simply be applied to the given number-field vector or a possibly singular evaluation point. The authors remove singularities and dependencies, then construct a Galois product whose normal-basis rational components form a closed rational differential system and whose evaluated combination has integer coefficients. Tracking the nonzero product, coefficient houses and non-Galois coset action completes a source-specific descent construction beyond merely applying a field norm inequality.

title: Holder stability of the vertex-coordinate Dirichlet eigenvalue shape Hessian and its spectrum near a fixed regular polygon with at least five sides
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.250
difficulty_reason: Ordinary domain continuity in H1 does not control the shape-Hessian coefficients, because the material-derivative equations have singular right-hand sides and eigenspace orthogonality constraints. The authors obtain stronger polygon-uniform regularity, estimate the varying right-hand sides and build projection corrections while controlling the material derivatives and coefficient blocks. Those new analytic estimates supply the Holder modulus before the routine finite-dimensional Weyl eigenvalue bound, rather than treating Weyl's theorem as the difficult obligation.

title: Polyhedral hyperbola asymptotics when the maximal-sum face is not contained in any coordinate hyperplane
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.251
difficulty_reason: The usual one-constraint hyperbola identity does not count boxes in a general polytope or control small-coordinate regions under box PropertyI alone. The authors prove volume and coordinate-projection bounds near the maximizing face, approximate weighted slice counts by lattice counting and separate dyadic interior and boundary contributions. This new polyhedral decomposition yields both the exact leading constant and the logarithmic saving without the stronger lower-dimensional-box assumption, beyond merely applying Davenport's lemma.

title: Transverse conformal volume expansion forces topological entropy on a compact foliated manifold
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.252
difficulty_reason: Transverse volume growth alone does not give an entropy bound when images of a transversal can return through many plaques. The authors construct a uniform leafwise-distance comparison and a finite product-chart partition, then prove that each dynamical itinerary intersects every terminal plaque at most once. This new geometric control gives a uniform volume bound per itinerary and forces exponentially many itineraries, rather than relying on the smoother Yomdin volume-growth theorem.

title: Every non-neat nonconstant periodic orbit of a smooth Hamiltonian with positive definite fiber Hessian is a round trip
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.255
difficulty_reason: Local uniqueness of Hamiltonian trajectories does not classify all returns of their projections to the base, and a non-neat orbit can contain both degenerate and self-intersection times. The author rules out transverse self-intersections globally, uses the energy-preserving fiber symmetry to construct a decreasing involution on every nondegenerate interval, and closes the time circle at the two turning points. The square-root coordinate then gives smoothness through the turning points, providing the new global round-trip classification beyond the ordinary local implicit-function theorem.

title: Independent Brownian continuum trees almost surely admit no Holder homeomorphism with exponent sufficiently close to one
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.256
difficulty_reason: A homeomorphism can align branch points adaptively, so mismatch at one random branch or a fixed map does not give a simultaneous obstruction for all homeomorphisms. The authors control exponentially many admissible branch-point chains and use a corrected positive-martingale mismatch argument to force uniform loss of region mass across recursive scales. Only after that new probabilistic core do Brownian excursion regularity and region-diameter bounds convert the mass loss into the strict Holder obstruction.

title: Countable bubble decomposition with conservation of bubbling mass for bounded positive measures
source_version: Journal de l'Ecole polytechnique - Mathematiques 11 (2024),431--472; published2024-02-19; original Theorem 3.2, printed 448--452 / physical PDF 19--23; official native/PDF hashes pinned
difficulty_reason: Banach-Alaoglu compactness and Portmanteau inequalities only yield local vague limits and allow mass to escape; they do not provide one subsequence with countably many simultaneously separated profiles. The authors construct nested extractions, a diagonal family of expanding balls and quantitative mass errors, then control every translated limit of the remainder by a decreasing bubbling quantity. They finally recenter each bubble in the support of the original measure while preserving narrow convergence and the whole bubbling-mass sum, which is nonroutine beyond qualifying-examination measure compactness.

title: Unconditional joint-moment asymptotics for Legendre paths averaged over dyadic prime intervals
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique—Mathématiques 11(2024),589–611; published2024-05-22; DOI10.5802/jep.260
difficulty_reason: After the ordinary Pólya expansion and prime-character prerequisites, the proof shortens all joint Fourier factors simultaneously outside an exponentially small exceptional set. It separates square, non-square and possible Landau–Siegel exceptional squareclasses with weighted divisor bounds. The ineffective Siegel lower bound then yields unconditional joint moments with arbitrary logarithmic savings, beyond ordinary doctoral analytic-number-theory qualifiers.

title: Lattice generation of Lipschitz functions over divisible ordered abelian groups
difficulty_reason: After ordinary DOAG model completeness and the cited special linear cell decomposition, the authors still prove parameter descent, a lattice-combination characterization and a separating hyperplane construction for closed cells. The main proof then inducts on nontrivial convex subgroups, passes to a quotient and constructs cell-pair functions bounding the given Lipschitz function on opposite sides. This new parameter-sensitive non-Archimedean separation and lattice-generation argument is substantially beyond ordinary doctoral qualification exercises.

title: Nonplanar smooth limits of complex plane curves whose degree is a multiple of a largest Markov-triple entry
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.263
difficulty_reason: Knowing that a weighted projective plane smooths to the plane does not extend the needed divisor class or guarantee a smooth member of its linear system on the partial smoothing. The authors control extension obstructions, compute the class/Picard and intersection scaling, and prove global generation and cohomology constancy for the relevant divisorial sheaves. Those new deformation and section-lifting results construct the smooth limit and its low-degree pencil before the standard gonality comparison, beyond merely applying the known Manetti surface classification.

title: Nonisomorphic projective hypersurfaces with isomorphic complements in degrees prime to the field characteristic
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.264
difficulty_reason: An affine cylinder isomorphism does not automatically descend to an isomorphism of projective complements, and it says nothing about whether the removed projective hypersurfaces are isomorphic. The authors construct inverse polynomial formulas with controlled homogeneous degree classes, then distinguish the hypersurfaces using singular local rings and maximal-multiplicity exceptional divisors through higher-dimensional cones. These new descent and geometric-invariant arguments are necessary before the final case split, beyond the classical cyclic-quotient or blow-up foundations alone.

title: Uniform polynomial approximation bounds for transcendental real numbers in degrees at least three
source_version: Journal de l’école polytechnique — Mathématiques11(2024),769–807, publisher version DOI10.5802/jep.265; nativeSHA6680ea954fc1e0841d16173395d68cfa1b19052ac3db70d409281738fab7e411
difficulty_reason: 以经典 resultant 估计、Gel’fond 高度引理和极小多项式背景作为先修后，作者仍需证明独立性转换索引集无限，并在三个连续转换 h<i<j 之间同步两个不同二维多项式格的高度与小值量。进一步通过移位多项式张成空间构造非零 (2n-1) 阶整数行列式，把跨转换高度约束转为 limsup 二次不等式；n=3 的根比较与 n≥4 的矛盾均属于同一完整参数族，不能替换为单次经典二多项式 resultant。

title: Parity-sharp polyhomogeneous mapping of weighted geodesic X-ray transforms on nontrapping manifolds with strictly convex boundary
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.266
difficulty_reason: A direct use of the ordinary pushforward theorem overestimates the boundary index set and does not recover the selected scattering-even support. The authors build a resolved geodesic double b-fibration and compatible scattering coordinates, then establish the involution symmetry of the coefficient integrals that removes odd powers of the geodesic length. That new geometric and parity core identifies the transformed exponent/log support, beyond merely invoking the allowed polyhomogeneous calculus foundations.

title: Minimal-exponent characterization of higher rational singularities for complex local complete intersections
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.267
difficulty_reason: The earlier numerical criterion for k-Du Bois singularities has a non-strict boundary and does not identify the lowest weight local-cohomology piece with the required intersection-complex Hodge module. The authors use duality to compare Hodge, order and weight filtrations and prove the necessary filtration-level isomorphisms in both directions, using the higher-codimension V-filtration Koszul description. This new comparison makes rationality equivalent to a strict minimal-exponent inequality, beyond simply quoting Saito's framework or the prior Du Bois criterion.

title: A proper smooth model on an analytic neighborhood yields a local meromorphic rational point
difficulty_reason: The argument constructs a strict affinoid neighborhood and a regular curve model whose specialization fiber simultaneously preserves the analytic neighborhood and realizes its bounded-function ring as a complete two-dimensional regular local ring. Its new local core then descends rational points through two successive discrete valuation rings and applies Hensel lifting, using the precise compatibility of their valuations with the ground field. Standard properness and Hensel lemmas alone do not supply that analytic-to-local-algebra construction; the full authored construction and nested auxiliary proofs are preserved and exceed ordinary PhD qualification exercises.

title: Finitely generated plane Cremona subgroups consisting entirely of algebraic elements have uniformly bounded degree
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.271
difficulty_reason: The known rational-fibration alternative does not bound a finitely generated algebraic subgroup preserving a fibration, because its elements may affect different fibers. The authors identify the Jonquieres complex with a restricted product of fiber trees and prove that purely elliptic finite-generation actions fix a common point, controlling persistent fibers in both abelian and semisimple north-south cases. That new fixed-point core supplies boundedness after the classical Cremona and local-field prerequisites, beyond merely applying the fibration classification.

title: Energy-decreasing convexification of free-boundary regions for nonnegative BV graphs over bounded convex planar domains
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.273
difficulty_reason: Taking a convex hull can change BV graph traces and can merge several admissible free-boundary regions, so ordinary convexity and lower semicontinuity do not show that the relaxed energy decreases. The authors derive a graph-current slice estimate for the new trace costs and apply countably many gap-filling operations with controlled area loss, then run a finite merging procedure and rebuild the prescribed endpoint curves. Those new constructive estimates close the nonclosed admissible class while preserving its boundary data, beyond merely applying standard BV compactness.

title: Dense commensurators of infinite normal lattice subgroups also commensurate the ambient irreducible lattice in characteristic zero
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.274
difficulty_reason: The usual finite-index-subgroup counting argument fails when the infinite normal subgroup is not finitely generated. The authors use the locally finite Cayley-Abels graph to construct a finite-index subgroup as a finite-ball stabilizer and prove that its fibers are invariant under the whole lattice. This new normalization construction then lets discrete normalizers force the two ambient lattices to be commensurable, beyond the classical rigidity and normalizer prerequisites alone.

title: Uniform finite-time vanishing-viscosity convergence for Lipschitz aggregation potentials with well-prepared probability data
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.275
difficulty_reason: Weak compactness alone does not identify the nonlinear interaction force when mass concentrates at atoms and the Lipschitz potential has a nondifferentiable diagonal. The authors symmetrize that interaction, pass both dissipative terms through the viscosity limit and use equality in the limiting energy inequality to recover the exact velocity field with zero diagonal convention. This new nonlinear measure-level identification closes the aggregation equation, beyond the standard Wasserstein compactness or gradient-flow foundations.

title: Semistable rank-five orthogonal flat connections on complex curves with no gr-semistable orthogonal Hodge filtration
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.276
difficulty_reason: The cited orthogonal-connection criterion alone does not produce a connection on the chosen nonsplit tensor product: the authors exclude every positive-degree isotropic decomposition, using stability and a splitting contradiction for the rank-two case. They then identify its stable rank-two destabilizer and show that connection invariance of its perpendicular would force a forbidden degree-zero connection. The new quasi-filtration obstruction and odd-rank filtration equivalence transfer that obstruction to every gr-semistable orthogonal filtration, beyond the allowed bundle and connection foundations.

title: Low-degree branched projective structures form a universal affine bundle over a family of branching classes
difficulty_reason: The affine-bundle conclusion depends on constructing relative branched projective atlases with prescribed branching class and identifying their differences through a relative Schwarzian equation. The new core forms an obstruction section via the Leray exact sequence, proves local holomorphic nonemptiness, and constructs a tautological universal family compatible with pullback. Serre duality supplies only the final low-degree vanishing; it does not supply these relative geometric constructions, which are retained in full and exceed ordinary PhD qualification exercises.

title: Unirationality of the complex moduli space of double covers of genus-five curves branched at four points
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.280
difficulty_reason: The standard Nikulin/K3 and quadric facts do not identify a dominant rational parameter space for the genus21 marked surface family. The authors reconstruct the three-quadric net from an elliptic pencil and bisecants, force its fourth exceptional curve, and then use an irreducible rational pencil member to produce the rational parameterization. Their explicit boundary deformation interchanges the two distinguished lattice classes and closes marked-cover irreducibility, supplying the new geometric obligation beyond the cited surface and compactification foundations.

title: Uniform exponential moments for first-exit particles of nondegenerate critical branching random walks with exponential offspring moments
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.281
difficulty_reason: A BGW exponential-moment bound by itself does not control the number of particles frozen at a spatial boundary, because repeated interior generations and spatial displacement remain coupled. The authors first contract the killed tree in generation blocks, then construct a quadratic spatial martingale linking its occupation to the frozen boundary population and control that martingale with the new killed-occupation estimate. The exit-probability and exponential-expansion steps then give the uniform squared-radius and sharper interior-start assertions, beyond standard BGW and random-walk prerequisites.

title: Smooth exterior self-similar profiles near the singular supercritical wave profile with weighted and parameter bounds
difficulty_reason: The construction requires an exterior resolvent that remains controlled across the singular light cone and simultaneously at the origin and infinity in distinct weighted norms. Its new local core computes fundamental-solution asymptotics and proves nonlinear Lipschitz estimates strong enough to construct the profile, its scaling derivative, and its parameter derivative. Banach contraction alone does not supply those singular weighted estimates or the smoothness argument across the light cone; the entire authored construction is retained and exceeds ordinary PhD qualification exercises.

title: Plante-like wreath-product actions and their finitely generated epimorphic lifts cannot be semi-conjugate to C1 actions on the closed interval
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique—Mathématiques 12(2025),23–69; published2024-12-13; DOI10.5802/jep.284
difficulty_reason: Beyond ordinary interval derivatives and group-order prerequisites, the proof builds Plante actions by dynamical realization of Laurent-polynomial lexicographic orders and establishes their nested support laminations and minimality. It constructs exponentially many pairwise-disjoint image intervals with controlled group words. Endpoint flattening, semiconjugacy and derivative lower bounds force an impossible total length, including finitely generated epimorphic lifts, beyond ordinary doctoral dynamics qualifiers.

title: Falconer-Lyapunov dimension variational principle for faithful Zariski-dense partially Anosov representations of non-elementary hyperbolic groups
difficulty_reason: H3 residual after the explicitly cited growth-indicator, finite proximality and Morse background: construct a quasi-geodesic semigroup with bounded two-sided correction, then refine exponentially many long elements into equal-length, free, uniformly diagonalizable generators with a common nearby splitting without losing growth entropy. The new local core must preserve singular-value direction for every product and entropy simultaneously, giving measures with h(mu_k)/T_k -> psi(a) and lambda(rho_*mu_k)/T_k -> a for general partial P-Anosov representations; the finite proximality theorem or the Borel-only variational result alone does not supply this construction.

title: Narrow relaxation of uniform connected one-dimensional measure length in ambient dimension at least two
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.286
difficulty_reason: Ordinary Hausdorff-length lower semicontinuity does not identify the narrow relaxation because weak limits can carry excess mass beyond uniform arclength. The authors combine a localized measure-valued Golab bound with a recovery sequence that realizes every cube excess by tiny nonoverlapping branches while preserving connectedness and exact total length. That new geometric recovery also enforces the measure convergence, supplying the remaining nonroutine relaxation obligation beyond the allowed compactness and rectifiability foundations.

title: Strict positive control threshold for minimal-time uniform Landau–Lifshitz magnetization reversal in ellipsoids with a simple easy axis
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique—Mathématiques 12(2025),147–184; published2025-01-17; DOI10.5802/jep.287
difficulty_reason: Beyond ordinary controlled-ODE existence and compactness, the proof obtains quantitative perturbation barriers around the easy-axis equilibrium, treating real, complex and repeated spectral cases. It couples this robust invariant hemisphere with an exact local finite-time steering construction near the opposite equilibrium. Openness of the finite-reversal control set excludes attainability even at its positive infimum, a global control-and-stability argument beyond ordinary doctoral ODE qualifiers.

title: Boundary-strong helix-box Birkhoff sections with prescribed primitive transverse classes for torus-invariant flows
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.289
difficulty_reason: The distinct primitive boundary homology classes require a controlled multiple cover of the interior binding, which an ordinary transverse annulus cannot provide. The authors construct and glue an explicit helicoidal quotient surface, prove its transversality by a derivative calculation and handle both signs of the binding coefficient. They then remove tangencies on the normal blow-up to obtain the required boundary-strong section, supplying the nonroutine geometric construction beyond standard surface topology.

title: Automatic split-generation and the quantum-cohomology factor from a smooth Lagrangian endomorphism algebra
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique—Mathématiques 12 (2025), 287–318; DOI 10.5802/jep.290; published 2025-02-18
difficulty_reason: The seven conclusions are connected by the Shklyarov pairing, open–closed isometry, weak proper Calabi–Yau duality, and the Hochschild module action. The proof constructs the two-sided quantum-cohomology factors Q and Q-perp, identifies the closed–open kernel, and proves split-generation by the resulting idempotent through Abouzaid’s criterion. Smoothness, Morita invariance and these categorical compatibility arguments exceed ordinary PhD qualifying-exam symplectic topology, while their cited standard foundations are kept distinct from Smith’s source-local construction.

title: Uniform sup-norm control for mean-zero bounded-Laplacian functions in cohomologically dominated degenerating Kähler families with Lp volume densities
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.291
difficulty_reason: A bounded Laplacian and zero mean do not yield a family-uniform oscillation bound from the available estimates without additional density control. The authors normalize by the unknown L1 size, compare positive and negative parts with twisted Monge–Ampère potentials, and close a small-Laplacian bootstrap that forces the normalization parameter away from zero. That new comparison/contradiction step supplies the missing uniform bound beyond the cited pluripotential foundations, without adding the discarded density hypothesis.

title: Geometric l-adic local systems on punctured smooth projective finite-field curves that no family of abelian varieties can generate
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.292
difficulty_reason: Tensor generation by abelian families permits large slopes in their tensor objects, so raw slopes of the proposed local system do not provide the required obstruction. The authors pass to the functorial monodromy Lie-local-system, bound its slopes through a Tannakian quotient, and apply that new obstruction to the ordinary invariant-summand/adjoint examples in every characteristic before pulling back to the chosen curve. This generation obstruction is the remaining nonroutine step; the source's monodromy, ordinarity, comparison and Hodge inputs are precise prior prerequisites, and the final slope tables alone are not the difficulty rationale.

title: Finite-dimensional added-inertia ODE reduction for volume-preserving toroidal solids in axisymmetric irrotational no-swirl Euler flow
difficulty_reason: Beyond ordinary elliptic, Newtonian-potential and fixed-test-function variational prerequisites, the proof reconstructs the unbounded axisymmetric no-swirl fluid from weighted potentials and circulation streamfunctions. It proves their shape differentiability and locally uniform decay, justifies all pressure integrations at infinity, and identifies the circulation-force, gyroscopic, added-inertia and Christoffel contributions. This complete volume-preserving nonrigid fluid–solid reduction is beyond ordinary doctoral PDE qualifiers.

title: Non-escape from uniformly expanding finite orbits under C2 random diffeomorphisms with logarithmic moments of order above one
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.294
difficulty_reason: The prior Margulis occupation theorem does not provide the needed drift from tangent expansion alone under a logarithmic moment of order just above one. The authors build the logarithmic-distance function and combine a bounded-map second-order Taylor comparison with a separate large-norm moment-tail estimate, choosing the neighborhood and cutoff so both errors preserve the expansion drift. This nonlinear drift construction is the remaining nonroutine step beyond the precise prior occupation theorem; no stronger exponential-moment assumption is introduced.

title: Vanishing minimal volume entropy for finite simplicial complexes with fiber growth strictly below the codimension ratio
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.295
difficulty_reason: Fiberwise contraction does not by itself control entropy because short loops can repeatedly leave fibers while the metric degenerates. The authors construct face-coherent Lipschitz retractions on uniform neighborhoods and prove an arc-to-edge deformation with a length constant independent of the collapsing parameter. They then count the interleaved long edges and fiber paths using subgroup growth to obtain the required entropy bound, which combines with volume scaling to give the strict codimension threshold.

title: Arbitrary-order depletion-layer expansion for the continuous half-space Stokes model with smooth compactly supported data up to the interface
difficulty_reason: After standard half-space Stokes solvability/regularity and thin-layer Poincare/trace estimates, the remaining construction couples bulk profiles with rescaled depletion-layer profiles through velocity, normal-divergence and stress matching at every fixed order. title: Curvature criterion for lifting first-order formal projective-metrizability jets to second order
source_version: SIGMA 7 (2011), article 114, published version of record; official EMIS Brno native/PDF bytes exactly match historical publisher pins; acquired 2026-10-03

title: Global univalence of the ergodic cylinder transformation on a periodic time scale (Theorem 3.5)

title: Pricing callable bonds and optimal callable time under the fractional Black-Scholes market: L1 consistency of the deep-learning price estimator (Theorem 3.6)

title: Infinitely many prescribed-frequency solutions of perturbed Schrodinger-Bopp-Podolsky systems in bounded domains: the critical-point Proposition 3.6

title: Global existence and the uniform a priori estimate in homogeneous Besov spaces for the 2D inviscid magnetic Benard system (Theorem 1.1)

It must first extract a horizontal dissipation term for the velocity from the temperature equation and a vertical dissipation term from the magnetic equation, through the cancellation identities (3.4), (3.6), (3.7) and (3.8) (source lines 544--609); then combine those four frequency-localized identities with two large constants C1 and C2 into the augmented energy functionals and prove their coercivity against the negative cross terms by Bernstein inequality in the two frequency regimes j at most 0 and j at least -1 (lines 611--666 and 729--777); then sum over the dyadic blocks in the two Besov norms and bound every nonlinear and commutator term by the product of the two energy functionals (lines 677--693 and 850--884); and finally close the Lyapunov-type differential inequality (3.26) under the smallness condition on the supremum of the energy, which is what forces the life span to be infinite by the bootstrap argument (lines 887--908). title: Existence of a positive solution for a generalized quasilinear Schrodinger equation with asymptotically linear nonlinearity via the Nehari manifold (Theorem 1.1)

Because the nonlinearity is only asymptotically linear, the mountain-pass geometry alone cannot produce a nontrivial solution and the fixed-sign Nehari manifold is not a manifold, so the authors work on the Nehari manifold split into two pieces through the auxiliary function and the map n, and the proof must (i) treat the easy cases through Propositions 3.14 and 3.15, where Ekeland variational principle is legitimised on the constrained set by the lemma preventing the limiting point from reaching the boundary (line 842), and where the concentration-compactness lemma for Palais-Smale sequences together with the norm equivalence turns the weak limit into a strong one (lines 847--850 and 884--895); (ii) in the remaining case, where the barycentric infimum is strictly larger than the limiting level, construct the modified path built from the dilation parameter and the scaling that returns the translated ground state to the Nehari manifold, whose properties are exactly Lemmas 3.16 to 3.20, including the reformulation of hypothesis (A11) as an interval condition and the strict inequality for the path level (lines 1007--1084); and (iii) run a deformation argument on the Nehari manifold to build a continuous map of a ball into its own boundary that is the identity on the boundary, a contradiction of the quoted topological fact (lines 1090--1110), after which sign-definiteness, elliptic regularity and the maximum principle upgrade the critical point to a positive solution (lines 1111--1113). title: Global asymptotic stability of the infection equilibrium of a delayed HIV model with CTL immune response and immune impairment (Theorem 3.4)

title: Functoriality of framed equivariant instanton homology on the weakly admissible U(2)-cobordism category
